title.zh: 卷七十九 列傳第三十九 文五王
title.raw: 卷七十九 列傳第三十九 文五王 Volume 79 Biographies 39: Wen Wuwang

sentences.zh: 列傳第三十九 文五王

translations.literal: Biography 39: The Five Princes of Emperor Wen
translations.idiomatic: Biography 39: The Five Princes of Emperor Wen

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕 廬江王禕 武昌王渾 海陵王休茂 桂陽王休範

translations.literal: Prince of Jingling, Dan; Prince of Lujiang, Yi; Prince of Wuchang, Hun; Prince of Hailing, Xiumao; Prince of Guiyang, Xiufan
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Jingling, Prince Yi of Lujiang, Prince Hun of Wuchang, Prince Xiumao of Hailing, and Prince Xiufan of Guiyang

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕，字休文，文帝第六子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingling Dan, styled Xiuwen, was the sixth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan of Jingling, whose courtesy name was Xiuwen, was the sixth son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，年十一，封廣陵王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia, when he was eleven, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，監南兗州諸軍事、北中郎將、南兗州刺史，出鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he supervised the military affairs of Southern Yan Province, served as General Who Pacifies the North, and was Governor of Southern Yan, going out to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made supervisor of military affairs in Southern Yan, General Who Pacifies the North, and governor of that province, and took up his post at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 尋以本號徙南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, retaining the same title, he was transferred to be Governor of Southern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, while keeping the same rank, he was transferred to govern Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，出為都督雍、梁、南北秦四州、荊州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、後將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he went out as Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Yong, Liang, the two Qins north and south, and the Jingzhou commanderies of Jingling and Sui, Rear General, and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was sent out as commander over Yong, Liang, Northern and Southern Qin, and the Jingzhou districts of Jingling and Sui, with the rank of Rear General and the governorship of Yong.

sentences.zh: 以廣陵彫弊，改封隨郡王。

translations.literal: Because Guangling was exhausted and impoverished, his fief was changed to Prince of Suixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangling had been worn down and impoverished, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Suixiang.

sentences.zh: 上欲大舉北討，以襄陽外接關、河，欲廣其資力，乃罷江州軍府，文武悉配雍州，湘州入台稅租雜物，悉給襄陽。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to launch a major northern campaign; because Xiangyang bordered the passes and the Yellow River, he wanted to expand its resources, so he abolished the Jiangzhou military headquarters, assigned all its civil and military personnel to Yongzhou, and sent all miscellaneous taxes and goods from Xiangzhou to the capital to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned a major northern campaign. Because Xiangyang lay on the frontier toward the passes and the Yellow River, he sought to strengthen it: he abolished the Jiangzhou military headquarters and reassigned all its officials and troops to Yongzhou, and diverted Xiangzhou's tax levies and assorted goods from the capital to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 及大舉北伐，命諸蕃並出師，莫不奔敗；

translations.literal: When the great northern expedition was launched, all the princely domains were ordered to take the field, and none failed to flee in defeat;
translations.idiomatic: When the great northern expedition was launched, every princely command was ordered to take the field, and all ended in rout;

sentences.zh: 唯誕中兵參軍柳元景先克弘農、關、陝三城，多獲首級，關、洛震動，事在元景傳。

translations.literal: only Dan's Central Army Major Liu Yuanjing first captured the three cities of Hongnong, Guan, and Shan, took many heads, and the Guan and Luo regions were shaken—the account is in Yuanjing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: only Liu Yuanjing, a staff officer on Dan's central army, first took Hongnong and the passes at Guan and Shan, capturing many heads and shaking the Guan and Luo region; the full account is in Yuanjing's biography.

sentences.zh: 會諸方並敗退，故元景引還。

translations.literal: As all sectors alike retreated in defeat, Yuanjing therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When every front had collapsed and pulled back, Yuanjing withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 徵誕還京師，遷都督廣、交二州諸軍事、安南將軍、廣州刺史，當鎮始興，未行；

translations.literal: Dan was summoned back to the capital and promoted to Commander-in-Chief of Guang and Jiao, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Guang, to garrison Shixing, but he did not go;
translations.idiomatic: Dan was recalled to the capital and appointed commander over Guang and Jiao, General Who Pacifies the South, and governor of Guang, with orders to garrison Shixing, but he never took up the post;

sentences.zh: 改授都督會稽、東陽、新安、臨海、永嘉五郡諸軍事、安東將軍、會稽太守，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Commander-in-Chief of the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Kuaiji, and granted one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he was made commander over Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, General Who Pacifies the East, and governor of Kuaiji, with a full ceremonial guard of pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以揚州浙江西屬司隸校尉，浙江東五郡立會州，以誕為刺史。

translations.literal: When the usurper seized the throne by regicide, the western Zhe River in Yangzhou was placed under the Director of the Retainers, the five eastern Zhe commanderies were made into Kuai Province, and Dan was made its governor.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurper Liu Shao murdered his way to the throne, the western half of the Zhe River region in Yangzhou was placed under the Director of the Retainers, the five eastern Zhe commanderies were organized as Kuai Province, and Dan was made its governor.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討，遣沈慶之兄子僧榮間報誕，又遣寧朔將軍顧彬之自魯顯東入，受誕節度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched in to suppress him, he sent Shen Qingzhi's nephew Seng Rong by secret message to inform Dan, and also sent General Who Pacifies the North Gu Binzhi east from Luxian to serve under Dan's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched east to suppress Shao, he sent Shen Qingzhi's nephew Seng Rong with a secret message to Dan, and dispatched General Who Pacifies the North Gu Binzhi east from Luxian to serve under Dan's command.

sentences.zh: 誕遣參軍劉季之與彬之並勢，自頓西陵，以為後繼。

translations.literal: Dan sent his staff officer Liu Jizhi to join forces with Binzhi, while he himself encamped at Xiling as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent his aide Liu Jizhi to combine forces with Binzhi, while he himself held Xiling as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 劭遣將華欽、庾導東討，與彬之弟相逢于曲阿之奔牛塘，路甚狹，左右皆悉入菰封，彬之軍人多齎籃屐，於菰葑中夾射之，欽等大敗。

translations.literal: Shao sent the generals Hua Qin and Yu Dao east to attack; they met Binzhi's younger brother at Ben Niu Pond in Qu'e. The road was very narrow and both flanks were thick with reed marshes. Many of Binzhi's soldiers carried basket-shoes; shooting from amid the reed beds on both sides, they inflicted a great defeat on Qin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Hua Qin and Yu Dao east to attack. They met Binzhi's younger brother at Ben Niu Pond near Qu'e, where the road was narrow and reed marshes closed in on both sides. Binzhi's men, many wearing basket-shoes, fired from the reeds on either flank and routed Qin's force completely—the victory later known as Ben Niu.

sentences.zh: 事平，征誕為持節、都督荊、湘、雍、益、寧、梁、南北秦八州諸軍事、衛將軍、開府儀同三司、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Dan was summoned as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the eight provinces of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and the two Qins north and south, Defender General, with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, Dan was summoned to court with the staff of command, made commander over Jing, Xiang, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, Defender General, with an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Jing.

sentences.zh: 誕以位號正與浚同，惡之，請求回改。

translations.literal: Dan, because his title and rank were exactly the same as Jun's, disliked this and requested a change.
translations.idiomatic: Dan found that his title and rank matched those of Prince Jun exactly and took offense, asking that they be altered.

sentences.zh: 乃進號驃騎將軍，加班劍二十人，餘如故。

translations.literal: He was then advanced to General of Agile Cavalry, with twenty guards bearing swords added, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to General of Agile Cavalry with twenty sword-bearing guards, while his other privileges remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 南譙王義宣不肯就征，以誕為侍中、驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史，開府如故。

translations.literal: When Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan refused the summons, Dan was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Yangzhou, his establishment as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao refused to obey the summons to court, Dan was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and governor of Yangzhou, retaining his former establishment.

sentences.zh: 改封竟陵王，食邑五千戶。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Prince of Jingling with five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jingling with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 顧彬之以奔牛之功，封陽新縣侯，食邑千戶，季之零陽縣侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Gu Binzhi, for the merit of Ben Niu, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxin with a fief of one thousand households; Jizhi as Marquis of Lingyang with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory at Ben Niu, Gu Binzhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxin with one thousand households, and Liu Jizhi as Marquis of Lingyang with five hundred.

sentences.zh: 明年，義宣舉兵反，有荊、江、兗、豫四州之力，勢震天下。

translations.literal: The next year Yixuan raised troops in rebellion, with the strength of the four provinces of Jing, Jiang, Yan, and Yu, and his power shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yixuan rose in rebellion with the armies of Jing, Jiang, Yan, and Yu behind him, and his power seemed to shake the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 上即位日淺，朝野大懼；

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the throne only a short time, and court and countryside were greatly afraid;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had only lately ascended the throne, and fear gripped court and countryside alike;

sentences.zh: 上欲奉乘輿法物，以迎義宣，誕固執不可，然後處分。

translations.literal: the emperor wished to send the imperial carriage and regalia to welcome Yixuan; Dan firmly refused to allow this, and only then were measures taken.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor even considered sending out the imperial carriage and regalia to welcome Yixuan; Dan adamantly opposed this, and only then did the court settle on a course of resistance.

sentences.zh: 加誕節，仗士五十人，出入六門。

translations.literal: Dan was granted the staff of command, fifty armed guards, and passage through all six gates.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was granted the staff of command, fifty armed guards, and the right to pass through all six palace gates.

sentences.zh: 上流平定，誕之力也。

translations.literal: The pacification of the upper Yangzi was Dan's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification of the upper Yangzi was largely Dan's doing.

sentences.zh: 初討元兇，與上同舉兵，有奔牛之捷，至是又有殊勳。

translations.literal: In the first campaign against the usurper he had raised arms with the emperor and won the victory at Ben Niu; now he had again rendered outstanding service.
translations.idiomatic: In the first campaign against the usurper he had taken up arms alongside the emperor and won the victory at Ben Niu; now he had distinguished himself once more.

sentences.zh: 上性多猜，頗相疑憚。

translations.literal: The emperor was by nature very suspicious and came to regard him with considerable fear and distrust.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply suspicious by nature and grew wary of him.

sentences.zh: 而誕造立第舍，窮極工巧，園池之美，冠于一時。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Dan built mansions to the utmost of craftsmanship; the beauty of his gardens and ponds was unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Dan built mansions of extraordinary craftsmanship, with gardens and ponds whose beauty surpassed anything of the age.

sentences.zh: 多聚才力之士，實之第內，精甲利器，莫非上品，上意愈不平。

translations.literal: He gathered many men of talent and strength to fill his residence; fine armor and sharp weapons, none but of the highest grade—the emperor's mind grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered talented and capable men to fill his residence, stocked it with the finest armor and weapons, and the emperor's resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，乃出為使持節、都督南徐、兗二州諸軍事、太子太傅、南徐州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Southern Xu and Yan, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Governor of Southern Xu, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaojian he was sent out with the staff of command as commander over Southern Xu and Yan, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and governor of Southern Xu, while retaining his post as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 上以京口去都密邇，猶疑之。

translations.literal: Because Jingkou was very close to the capital, the emperor still suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jingkou lay so close to the capital, the emperor remained uneasy.

sentences.zh: 大明元年秋，又出為都督南兗、南徐、兗、青、冀、幽六州諸軍事、南兗州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Daming he was again sent out as Commander-in-Chief of the six provinces of Southern Yan, Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, and Governor of Southern Yan, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Daming he was transferred again as commander over Southern Yan, Southern Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You, and governor of Southern Yan, his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 誕既見猜，亦潛為之備，至廣陵，因索虜寇邊，修治城隍，聚糧治仗。

translations.literal: Dan, having come under suspicion, also secretly made preparations; reaching Guangling, he used the northern barbarians' raids on the border as a pretext to repair walls and moats and to gather grain and forge weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Once under suspicion, Dan began preparing in secret as well. At Guangling he used raids by the northern barbarians as a pretext to repair the walls and moats and to stockpile grain and arms.

sentences.zh: 嫌隙既著，道路常云誕反。

translations.literal: Once the rift was plain, people on the roads constantly said Dan would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: As the breach became obvious, rumor on every road had it that Dan was about to rebel.

sentences.zh: 三年，建康民陳文紹上書曰：「私門有幸，亡大姑元嘉中蒙入臺六宮，薄命早亡，先朝賜贈美人，又聽大姑二女出入問訊。

translations.literal: In the third year the Jiankang commoner Chen Wenshao submitted a memorial saying: "Our humble household was fortunate: my deceased elder aunt in Yuanjia was admitted to the Six Palaces of the Terrace; her ill-fated life ended early, and the former court granted her the title of Beauty. Her two daughters were also allowed to come and go with inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year a Jiankang commoner named Chen Wenshao submitted a memorial: "Our family was once fortunate: my late elder aunt entered the palace harem during Yuanjia; she died young, and the former court posthumously granted her the title of Beauty. Her two daughters were permitted to visit us with news from the palace.

sentences.zh: 父饒，司空誕取為府史，恆使入山圖畫道路，勤劇備至，不敢有辭，不復聽歸，消息斷絕。

translations.literal: My father Rao—the Minister of Works Dan took him as a clerk in his administration and constantly sent him into the mountains to map roads, with labor so extreme he dared not refuse; he was no longer allowed to return home, and all news was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: My father Rao was taken on as a clerk by Minister Dan and constantly sent into the mountains to survey roads. The labor was crushing and he dared not refuse; he was no longer allowed to go home, and we heard nothing from him.

sentences.zh: 姑二女去年冒啟歸訴，蒙陛下聖恩，賜敕解饒吏名。

translations.literal: The aunt's two daughters last year ventured to petition on returning home; by Your Majesty's sacred grace an edict was granted releasing Rao from his clerk's register.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the two daughters ventured to petition on their return home, and by Your Majesty's grace an edict was issued releasing Rao from official service.

sentences.zh: 誕見符至，大怒，喚饒入交問：『汝欲死邪？

translations.literal: When Dan saw the warrant arrive, he was furious, summoned Rao in for questioning, and said: 'Do you want to die?
translations.idiomatic: When Dan saw the edict arrive, he flew into a rage, summoned Rao, and demanded: "Do you want to die?

sentences.zh: 訴臺求解。』

translations.literal: Petitioning the Terrace for release?'
translations.idiomatic: Petitioning the court for release?"

sentences.zh: 饒即答：『官比不聽通家信，消息斷絕。

translations.literal: Rao at once answered: 'Your lordship lately would not allow letters to reach my family; all news was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Rao answered at once: "Your lordship would not allow any word to reach my family; we had heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 若是姊為啟聞，所不知。』

translations.literal: If my elder sisters made the petition, I do not know.'
translations.idiomatic: If my sisters made the petition, I knew nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 誕因問饒：『汝那得入臺？』

translations.literal: Dan then asked Rao: 'How did you get into the Terrace?'
translations.idiomatic: Dan then asked: "How did you ever enter the palace?"

sentences.zh: 饒被問，依實啟答。

translations.literal: Rao, questioned, answered truthfully according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Rao, pressed for an answer, told the truth.

sentences.zh: 既出，誕主衣莊慶、畫師王強語饒：『汝今年敗，汝姊誤汝。

translations.literal: After he left, Dan's master of robes Zhuang Qing and the painter Wang Qiang said to Rao: 'You are ruined this year; your sisters have ruined you.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, Dan's master of robes Zhuang Qing and the painter Wang Qiang told him: "You are finished this year; your sisters have destroyed you.

sentences.zh: 官云小人輩敢持臺家逼我。』

translations.literal: His lordship said these petty fellows dare use the Terrace household to press me.'
translations.idiomatic: The lord said these wretches dare use the palace household to pressure me."

sentences.zh: 饒因叛走歸，誕即遣王強將數人逐，突入家內縛錄，將還廣陵。

translations.literal: Rao therefore fled home in rebellion; Dan at once sent Wang Qiang with several men in pursuit, burst into the house, bound and seized him, and took him back toward Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Rao fled home, but Dan sent Wang Qiang with several men in pursuit. They burst into the house, seized him, and hauled him back toward Guangling.

sentences.zh: 至京口客舍，乃陊死井中，託云『饒懼罪自殺』。

translations.literal: At an inn in Jingkou he was thrown down a well to his death, with the excuse given that 'Rao, fearing punishment, killed himself.'
translations.idiomatic: At an inn in Jingkou he was thrown down a well and killed, with the story put about that "Rao, fearing punishment, took his own life."

sentences.zh: 抱痛懷冤，冒死歸訴。」

translations.literal: Clutching grief and nursing wrong, I risk death to return and plead."
translations.idiomatic: Bearing this grief and injustice, I risk death to bring this plea."

sentences.zh: 吳郡民劉成又詣闕上書，告誕謀反，稱：「息道龍昔伏事誕，親見姦狀。

translations.literal: The Wu commandery commoner Liu Cheng also went to the palace gate with a memorial accusing Dan of plotting rebellion, stating: "My son Dao Long formerly served Dan and personally witnessed his treacherous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Wu commandery named Liu Cheng also came to the palace with a memorial accusing Dan of rebellion. He wrote: "My son Dao Long once served Dan and saw his treachery with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: 又見誕在石頭城內，修乘輿法物，習倡警蹕。

translations.literal: He also saw Dan within Shitou city repairing the imperial carriage and regalia and practicing the music of warning and the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: He also saw Dan inside Shitou city preparing the imperial carriage and regalia and rehearsing the ceremonial music and progress of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 道龍私獨憂懼，向伴侶言之，語頗漏泄，誕使大吏令監內執道龍，道龍逸走，誕怒鞭殺監，又捕殺道龍。」

translations.literal: Dao Long alone was privately anxious and fearful; he spoke of it to his companions, and the words leaked somewhat. Dan had the chief clerk order the inner guard to seize Dao Long; Dao Long escaped. Dan in anger had the guard flogged to death and also hunted down and killed Dao Long.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Long confided his fears to his companions, and word leaked out. Dan ordered the chief clerk to have the inner guard seize him; Dao Long escaped. Dan had the guard flogged to death in his rage and then hunted down and killed Dao Long.

sentences.zh: 又豫章民陳談之上書訴枉，稱：「弟詠之昔蒙誕採錄，隨從歷鎮；

translations.literal: The Yuzhang commoner Chen Tan also submitted a memorial pleading injustice, stating: "My younger brother Yongzhi formerly received Dan's recruitment and followed him through his successive postings;
translations.idiomatic: A man of Yuzhang named Chen Tan also submitted a memorial of grievance: "My younger brother Yongzhi was once recruited by Dan and followed him through his successive postings;

sentences.zh: 大駕南下，為誕奉送箋書，經涉危險，時得上聞。

translations.literal: when the imperial carriage marched south, he bore Dan's letters of submission through dangers, and at the time was able to have them reported above.
translations.idiomatic: when the imperial army marched south, he carried Dan's letters of submission through great danger and managed to get word to the court.

sentences.zh: 聖明登阼，恩澤周普，回改小人，使命微勤，賜署臺位。

translations.literal: When the sage and bright one ascended the throne, grace spread everywhere; this petty man was turned and reformed, given a minor mission for slight diligence, and granted a post at the Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty ascended the throne, grace spread everywhere; this humble man was reformed, given a minor assignment for small service, and granted a post at court.

sentences.zh: 詠之恆見誕與左右小人莊慶、傅元祀潛圖姦逆，言詞醜悖，每云：『天下方是我家有，汝等不憂不富貴。』

translations.literal: Yongzhi constantly saw Dan with his petty attendants Zhuang Qing and Fu Yuansi secretly plotting treachery, with ugly and rebellious words, often saying: 'The realm under Heaven is just now our family's possession; you need not worry about lacking wealth and honor.'
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi constantly saw Dan with his cronies Zhuang Qing and Fu Yuansi secretly plotting treason, speaking in vile and rebellious terms, often saying: "The realm under Heaven is our family's to take; you need not worry about wealth or rank."

sentences.zh: 又常疏陛下年紀姓諱，往巫鄭師憐家祝詛。

translations.literal: He also often wrote out Your Majesty's age and name and taboo, and sent them to the shaman Zheng Shilian's household for curses and imprecations.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote out Your Majesty's age, name, and tabooed characters and sent them to the shaman Zheng Shilian's household for curses.

sentences.zh: 詠之既聞此語，又不見其事，恐一旦事發，橫罹其罪，密以告建康右尉黃宣達，并有啟聞，希以自免。

translations.literal: Yongzhi, having heard these words yet not witnessing the deed, feared that when the affair broke out he would suffer punishment in spite of himself; he secretly told the Right Commandant of Jiankang Huang Xuanda, and also submitted a report above, hoping thereby to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi heard these words but never saw the plot carried out; fearing that when matters came to a head he would be punished anyway, he secretly informed the Right Commandant of Jiankang, Huang Xuanda, and also sent a report to the court, hoping to save himself.

sentences.zh: 元祀弟知詠之與宣達來往，自嫌言語漏泄，即具以告誕。

translations.literal: Yuansi's younger brother learned of Yongzhi's dealings with Xuanda, feared his own words had leaked, and reported everything in full to Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansi's younger brother learned of Yongzhi's contact with Xuanda, feared that his own words had leaked, and reported everything to Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕大怒，令左右飲詠之酒，逼使大醉，因言詠之乘酒罵詈，遂被害。

translations.literal: Dan was furious, ordered his attendants to make Yongzhi drink wine and forced him to great drunkenness, then claimed Yongzhi had cursed and reviled while drunk, and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was furious. He had his men force wine on Yongzhi until he was drunk, then claimed Yongzhi had cursed and reviled him while intoxicated, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 自顧冤枉，事有可哀。」

translations.literal: Considering my own wronged innocence, the matter is pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on this injustice, the case is pitiable indeed."

sentences.zh: 其年四月，上乃使有司奏曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year the emperor had the relevant offices memorialize:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year the emperor ordered the relevant offices to submit a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞神極尊明，大儀所以貞觀；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the divine pole is supremely bright, the great norm thereby stands firm in observation;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when the divine pole shines with supreme clarity, the great norm of the realm stands firm;

sentences.zh: 皇天峻邈，玄化所以幽宣。

translations.literal: when August Heaven is lofty and far-reaching, the dark transformation is thereby subtly proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: when August Heaven towers in its remoteness, the hidden transformation of the Way is proclaimed in the depths.

sentences.zh: 故能經緯氓俗，大庇黔首。

translations.literal: Thus it can weave and order the customs of the people and broadly shelter the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the ruler can weave order through the customs of the people and shelter all the black-haired masses beneath his care.

sentences.zh: 庶道被八紘，不遺疏賤之賞；

translations.literal: So that the Way may spread over the eight cords of the earth, not omitting rewards even for the remote and lowly;
translations.idiomatic: So that the Way may reach the eight corners of the earth, withholding no reward even from the remote and lowly;

sentences.zh: 威格天區，豈漏親貴之罰。

translations.literal: and awe may reach the celestial regions—how could punishment be omitted for the near and noble?
translations.idiomatic: and awe may reach the heavens themselves—how could punishment be withheld from kin and nobles alike?

sentences.zh: 此不刊之鴻則，古今之恆訓。

translations.literal: This is the great constant that cannot be effaced, the everlasting teaching of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great and unchanging principle, the eternal teaching of past and present.

sentences.zh: 謹按元嘉之末，天綱崩褫，人神哀憤，含生喪氣。

translations.literal: Respectfully investigating: at the end of Yuanjia the celestial net collapsed and was torn away; men and spirits grieved and raged, and all who bore life lost their breath.
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully report: at the end of Yuanjia the celestial order collapsed; men and spirits alike grieved and raged, and all living things lost heart.

sentences.zh: 司空竟陵王誕義兼臣子，任居藩維。

translations.literal: Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling Dan, in duty both minister and son, held office at the frontier pillar of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dan, Prince of Jingling, bore the double duty of subject and son and held a frontier command at the realm's pillar.

sentences.zh: 進不能泣血提戈，忘身徇節；

translations.literal: Advancing, he could not weep blood and raise the spear, forgetting his person to follow righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: When he should have advanced, he did not weep blood and take up arms, forgetting himself in loyal service;

sentences.zh: 退不能閉關拒險，焚符斬使。

translations.literal: retreating, he could not shut the passes and hold the defiles, burn the credentials and behead the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: when he should have held back, he did not shut the passes, burn the credentials, and behead the envoys.

sentences.zh: 遂至拜受偽爵，欣承榮寵，沈淪姦逆，肆於昏放。

translations.literal: He went so far as to bow and accept the usurper's rank, gladly receiving glory and favor, sinking into treachery and rebellion, indulging in dissipation and license.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he bowed and accepted the usurper's titles, gladly receiving honors from a rebel court, and sank into treachery, dissipation, and license.

sentences.zh: 以妻故司空臣湛之女，誅亡余類，單舟遄遣，披猖千里，事哀行路，賊忍無親，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Because his wife was the daughter of the former Minister of Works Chen Zhan, whose kindred were executed and exterminated, he dispatched her alone in a single boat with all speed, raging across a thousand li—the affair grieved travelers on the road; in treachery and cruelty devoid of kin feeling, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Because his wife was the daughter of the executed Minister Chen Zhan, whose entire clan had been wiped out, he sent her off alone in a single boat at full speed across a thousand li—a sight that moved every traveler on the road. In treachery and cruelty toward his own kin, nothing could exceed this.

sentences.zh: 故山陰傅僧祐，誠亮國朝，義均休戚。

translations.literal: The late Fu Sengyou of Shanyin was loyal and bright toward the dynastic court, sharing fortune and misfortune alike.
translations.idiomatic: The late Fu Sengyou of Shanyin was loyal and upright toward the dynasty, sharing its fortunes and its perils.

sentences.zh: 重門峻衛，不能拒折簡之使；

translations.literal: Though his gates were many and his guards stern, he could not refuse the envoy bearing a simple letter;
translations.idiomatic: Though his gates were barred and his guards stern, he could not refuse the envoy bearing a summons;

sentences.zh: 岩險千里，不能庇匹夫之身。

translations.literal: though his cliffs and defiles stretched a thousand li, he could not shelter a single common man's person.
translations.idiomatic: though his cliffs and defiles stretched a thousand li, he could not protect a single common man's life.

sentences.zh: 乃更助虐憑凶，抽兵勒刃，遂使頓仆牢井，死不旋踵，妻子播流，庭筵莫立，見之者流涕，聞之者含歎。

translations.literal: He then further aided cruelty and relied on violence, drew out troops and forced blades, so that Sengyou was cast down into a prison well and died without turning his heel; wife and children were scattered, the household feast could not be set—those who saw it wept, those who heard it sighed.
translations.idiomatic: He then aided the tyrant further, drew troops and forced blades upon him, and cast him down a prison well to die on the spot. Wife and children were scattered, the household left in ruins—those who saw it wept, those who heard it sighed.

sentences.zh: 及神鋒首路，欃槍東指，風卷四嶽，電埽三江。

translations.literal: When the divine blade took the road and the comet pointed east, wind swept the four peaks and lightning scoured the three rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army took the field and the comet pointed east, wind swept the four sacred peaks and lightning scoured the three rivers.

sentences.zh: 誕猶持疑兩端，陰規進退。

translations.literal: Dan still wavered between two sides and secretly plotted advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Dan still wavered between two sides and secretly plotted whether to advance or hold back.

sentences.zh: 陛下頻遣書檄，告譬殷勤，方改姦圖，末乃奉順。

translations.literal: Your Majesty repeatedly sent letters and proclamations with earnest admonition; only then did he alter his treacherous designs and at last submit.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty sent letter after letter with earnest admonition; only then did he abandon his treacherous designs and at last submit.

sentences.zh: 分遣弱旅，永塞符文，宴安所蒞，身不越境，悖禮忘情，不顧物議，彎弧躍馬，務是畋遊，致奔牛有崩碎之陳，新亭無獨克之術。

translations.literal: He sent out only weak detachments and forever blocked the credentials; where ease and comfort were at hand, his person did not cross the border. Reckless of ritual, forgetful of feeling, heedless of public opinion, he bent the bow and leapt on horseback, bent only on hunting—so that at Ben Niu there was an array in collapse and at Xinting no means of victory by fighting alone.
translations.idiomatic: He sent only weak detachments and blocked the imperial credentials; though the campaign was at his doorstep, he would not cross his border. He defied ritual, ignored public opinion, bent his bow and leapt to horseback for the hunt alone—so that at Ben Niu the army was shattered and at Xinting there was no hope of victory fought alone.

sentences.zh: 假威義銳，乞命皇旅，竟有何勞，而論功伐。

translations.literal: Borrowing the prestige of Yixuan's sharpness, he begged mercy from the imperial host—what labor had he truly performed that merit should be discussed?
translations.idiomatic: Riding on Yixuan's strength, he begged mercy from the imperial army—what real labor had he done that merit should be claimed?

sentences.zh: 既妖祲廓清，大明升曜，幽顯宅心，遠邇雲集。

translations.literal: Once the demonic vapors were cleared away and the great brightness rose in splendor, the hidden and manifest took the throne to heart, and far and near gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Once the evil omens were cleared away and the great brightness of Daming rose, the seen and unseen alike gave their hearts to the throne, and far and near gathered like clouds.

sentences.zh: 誕忽星行之悲，違開泰之慶，遲回顧望，淹逾旬朔。

translations.literal: Dan suddenly affected the grief of a shooting star, defying the celebration of opening peace; he lingered and looked back, delaying more than a full month.
translations.idiomatic: Dan suddenly affected the grief of a falling star and defied the celebration of the new reign; he lingered and looked back, delaying more than a full month.

sentences.zh: 逆黨陳叔兒等，泉寶钜億，資貨不貲，誕收籍所得，不歸天府，辭稱天軍，實入私室。

translations.literal: The rebel party Chen Shuer and others had treasure in the hundreds of millions, goods beyond reckoning; Dan registered what he seized but did not return it to the imperial treasury, claiming it was for the heavenly army while in fact it entered his private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Chen Shuer and his followers held treasure in the hundreds of millions; Dan registered what he seized but did not return it to the imperial treasury, claiming it was for the imperial army while in fact it went into his private store.

sentences.zh: 又太官東傳，舊有獻御，喪亂既平，猶加斷遏，珍羞庶品，回充私膳。

translations.literal: Moreover the Eastern Kitchen relay of the Grand Steward, which by old custom presented offerings to the throne—though the turmoil of mourning and disorder was already pacified—he still cut off and blocked; delicacies and all sorts of goods were diverted to fill his private table.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he intercepted the Eastern Kitchen relay that by old custom presented delicacies to the throne—even after the turmoil had ended—and diverted its fine foods to his private table.

sentences.zh: 於號諱之辰，遽甘滋之品，當惟新之始，絕苞苴之貢，忠孝兩忘，敬愛俱盡。

translations.literal: On the days of mourning taboo he hastened to sweet and rich foods; at the beginning when all should be made new, he cut off the tribute of gifts—filial piety and loyalty were both forgotten, reverence and love both exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: On the days of mourning taboo he feasted on rich delicacies; at the beginning of the new reign he cut off tribute gifts—filial piety and loyalty alike forgotten, reverence and love alike cast aside.

sentences.zh: 乃徵引巫史，潛考圖緯，自謂體應符相，富貴可期，悖意醜言，不可勝載。

translations.literal: He then summoned shamans and clerks, secretly examined charts and weft texts, and declared himself bodily matched to the omens of rule, with wealth and honor to be expected—rebellious words and ugly speech beyond all recording.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned shamans and clerks, secretly examined prophetic texts, and declared that his body matched the omens of rule and that wealth and honor awaited him—rebellious and vile speech beyond all reckoning.

sentences.zh: 遂復遙諷朝廷，占求官爵，侮蔑宗室，詆毀公卿，不義不昵，人道將盡。

translations.literal: He then again mocked the court from afar, sought by divination offices and ranks, insulted the imperial clan, slandered the excellencies and ministers—unrighteous, without affection; the way of humanity was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked the court from afar, sought offices and ranks by divination, insulted the imperial clan, and slandered the high ministers—unrighteous and without natural affection; the way of humanity was nearly at an end.

sentences.zh: 荷任神州，方懷姦慝，每窺向宸御，妄生規幸；

translations.literal: Bearing office over the divine land, he was just then harboring treacherous malice, constantly peering toward the imperial residence and vainly cherishing schemes of fortune;
translations.idiomatic: Holding office over the heartland of the empire, he harbored treacherous designs, constantly peering toward the imperial residence and nursing vain hopes;

sentences.zh: 多樹淫祀，顯肆祅詛，遂在石頭，潛修法物；

translations.literal: he set up many illicit sacrifices, openly practiced demonic curses, and then at Shitou secretly prepared the regalia of rule;
translations.idiomatic: he set up illicit sacrifices, openly practiced demonic curses, and at Shitou secretly prepared the regalia of an emperor;

sentences.zh: 傳警稱蹕，擬則天行，皆已駭暴觀聽，彰布朝野。

translations.literal: proclaiming warnings and calling the imperial progress, modeling the march of Heaven—all this has already shocked and exposed itself to sight and hearing, spread plainly through court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: proclaiming warnings and rehearsing the imperial progress, modeling himself on the Son of Heaven—all of which has shocked every witness and spread plainly through court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 昔內難甫寧，珍瑋散佚，有御刀利刃，擅價諸夏，天府禁器，歷代所珍。

translations.literal: Formerly, when internal strife was just pacified, precious jades were scattered and lost; there were imperial blades and sharp swords that commanded prices throughout the Xia, treasures of the celestial storehouse cherished by successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: When the internal strife was just pacified, precious treasures were scattered and lost—including imperial blades and sharp swords prized throughout the realm, treasures of the imperial storehouse cherished by every dynasty.

sentences.zh: 誕密加購賞，頓藏私室。

translations.literal: Dan secretly added purchases and rewards and hoarded them all in his private chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Dan secretly bought them up and hoarded them in his private chambers.

sentences.zh: 賊義宣初平，餘黨逃命，誕含縱罔忌，私竊招納，名工細巧，悉匿私第。

translations.literal: When the rebel Yixuan was first pacified, remnant factions fled for their lives; Dan harbored and indulged without restraint, privately recruiting and accepting them; master craftsmen and fine artisans were all hidden in his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Yixuan was first defeated, his remnant followers fled for their lives; Dan sheltered them without restraint, secretly recruiting them, and hid master craftsmen in his private residence.

sentences.zh: 又引義宣故將裘興為己腹心，事既彰露，猶執欺罔，公文面啟，矯稱舊隸。

translations.literal: He also drew Yixuan's former general Qiu Xing as his intimate confidant; when the matter was already exposed, he still clung to deception—in an official document to the throne he falsely claimed Xing was an old retainer.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Yixuan's former general Qiu Xing as his intimate confidant; when this was exposed, he still lied—in an official memorial to the throne he falsely claimed Xing was an old retainer.

sentences.zh: 加以營幹制館，僭擬天居，引石征材，專擅興發，驅迫士族，役同輿皁，殫木土之姿，窮吞併之勢。

translations.literal: Moreover he undertook construction and built halls, usurping the model of the celestial dwelling; he drew stone and requisitioned timber, monopolizing all works and levies, driving and pressing the gentry clans, employing them like carriage lackeys, exhausting the resources of wood and earth, and pushing annexation to its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he undertook vast construction and built halls modeled on the imperial palace, requisitioning stone and timber at will, driving the gentry like carriage lackeys, exhausting every resource of wood and earth, and pushing annexation to its limit.

sentences.zh: 故會稽宣長公主受遇二祖，禮級尊崇，臣湛之亡身徇國，追榮典軍。

translations.literal: The late Princess Chang of Kuaiji Xuan received favor from the two founding emperors, with ritual rank held in honor; your servant Zhan gave his life for the state and was posthumously honored as Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: The late Princess Chang of Kuaiji had been honored by the two founding emperors with the highest ritual rank; Minister Chen Zhan gave his life for the state and was posthumously honored as Director of the Army.

sentences.zh: 誕以廣拓宅宇，地妨藝植，輒逼遺孤，頓相驅徙。

translations.literal: Dan, to broaden and extend his mansions, where the land obstructed plantings, abruptly pressed the orphaned survivors and drove them all to move.
translations.idiomatic: To expand his mansions, Dan pressed the orphaned survivors to move wherever his building plans required, driving them from their lands.

sentences.zh: 遂令神主宵遷，改卜委巷，宗戚含傷，行路掩涕。

translations.literal: He thus made the spirit tablets move by night, changing the divination to a mean lane; kinsmen bore grief, and travelers on the road covered their tears.
translations.idiomatic: He forced the ancestral tablets to be moved by night to a mean back alley; kinsmen grieved and travelers on the road wept.

sentences.zh: 又緣谿兩道，積代通衢，誕拓宇開垣，擅斷其一。

translations.literal: Moreover along the two roads by the stream, thoroughfares for generations, Dan expanded his domain and opened walls, arbitrarily cutting off one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover along two roads by the stream that had been public thoroughfares for generations, Dan expanded his walls and arbitrarily blocked one of them.

sentences.zh: 致使徑塗擁隔，川陸阻礙，神怒民怨，毒遍幽顯。

translations.literal: This caused direct paths to be blocked and choked, rivers and roads obstructed; spirits raged and the people resented, and poison spread through the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: This blocked the direct routes and obstructed river and land traffic; spirits and people alike raged, and outrage spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 故丞相臨川烈武王臣道規，名德茂親，勳光常策，異禮殊榮，受自先旨者。

translations.literal: The late Chancellor, Prince Martially Martial of Linchuan, your servant Daogui, of illustrious virtue and flourishing kinship, his merit shining in the eternal registers, received exceptional ritual and special honor by the former emperor's decree.
translations.idiomatic: The late Chancellor, Prince Daogui of Linchuan, was a kinsman of illustrious virtue whose merit shines in the eternal records; he received exceptional honors by the former emperor's decree.

sentences.zh: 嗣王臣義慶受任西夏，靈寢暫移，先帝親枉鑾輿，拜辭路左，恩冠終古，事絕常班。

translations.literal: The heir prince, your servant Yiqing, received appointment in Western Xia; when the spirit couch was temporarily moved, the late emperor personally bent the imperial carriage to bow and take leave by the roadside—favor surpassing all antiquity, a matter beyond ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yiqing was appointed in Western Xia; when the ancestral tomb was temporarily moved, the late emperor personally drove his carriage to bow and take leave by the roadside—an honor surpassing all antiquity.

sentences.zh: 誕又以廟居宅前，固請毀換，詔旨不許，怨懟彌極。

translations.literal: Dan again, because the temple stood before his residence, firmly requested its destruction and removal; the imperial edict did not permit this, and his resentment grew ever more extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Because a temple stood before his residence, Dan repeatedly demanded its demolition; when the edict refused, his resentment grew extreme.

sentences.zh: 有靦面目，豺狼為性，規牧江都，希廣兵力，天德尚弘，甫申所請，仍謂應住東府，宜為中台，貪冒無厭，人莫與比。

translations.literal: Shameless in face, wolfish in nature, he plotted to pasture Jiangdu and hoped to broaden his military strength; though heavenly virtue was still magnanimous and had just granted his request, he still claimed he ought to dwell in the Eastern Palace and should hold the Central Secretariat—greedy and insatiable, no one could be compared to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shameless and wolfish by nature, he schemed to hold Jiangdu and expand his armies; though the court had just granted his request, he still claimed he ought to dwell in the Eastern Palace and hold the Central Secretariat—greedy beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 雖聖慈全救，每垂容納，而虐戾不悛，姦詖彌甚。

translations.literal: Although sacred compassion fully preserved him and repeatedly showed forbearance, he did not repent of cruelty and violence, and treachery and slander grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor's compassion repeatedly spared and indulged him, he did not repent of his cruelty, and his treachery grew worse.

sentences.zh: 受命還鎮，猜怨愈深，忠規正諫，必加鴆毒，諂瀆膚躁，是與比周。

translations.literal: Ordered to return to his post, his suspicion and resentment grew deeper; loyal counsel and upright remonstrance he invariably met with poison; flatterers and the frivolous were his companions and confederates.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered back to his post, his suspicion deepened; loyal counsel he answered with poison, while flatterers became his closest companions.

sentences.zh: 又矯稱符敕，設榜開募，事發辭寢，委罪自下。

translations.literal: He also falsely claimed imperial credentials, set up placards to recruit openly; when the affair broke out he shifted his words and sleep, casting blame on subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He forged imperial credentials and posted recruitment notices; when exposed he changed his story and blamed subordinates.

sentences.zh: 及錄事徐靈壽以常署受坐，將就囚執，舀韓近恭，中護軍遣吏夏嗣伯密相屬請，求寬桎梏。

translations.literal: When the recorder Xu Lingshou, for routine office, was implicated and about to be seized and imprisoned, Han Jingong was summoned; the Director of the Guardians of the Heir Apparent sent the clerk Xia Sibo with secret entreaties to seek leniency in his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: When the recorder Xu Lingshou was implicated in a routine matter and about to be imprisoned, Han Jingong was summoned, and the Director of the Guardians of the Heir Apparent sent the clerk Xia Sibo with secret pleas to loosen his bonds.

sentences.zh: 且王僧達臨刑之啟事，高闍即戮之辭，皆稱潛驛往來，遙相要契，醜聲穢問，宣著遐邇，含識能言，孰不憤歎。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Sengda's memorial on the eve of execution and Gao Ge's words at immediate execution both claimed secret relay stations and distant mutual pledges; foul rumors and filthy reports were proclaimed far and near—who among the knowing and articulate did not rage and sigh?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Wang Sengda's final memorial and Gao Ge's words at execution both spoke of secret messages and distant conspiracies; foul rumors spread far and wide, and who among the knowing did not rage and sigh?

sentences.zh: 又獲吳郡民劉成、豫章民陳談之、建康民陳文紹等並如訴狀，則姦情猜志，歲月增積。

translations.literal: Moreover the Wu commoner Liu Cheng, the Yuzhang commoner Chen Tan, and the Jiankang commoner Chen Wenshao were all obtained, matching their petitions in every respect—thus treacherous intent and suspicious designs had accumulated over the years.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liu Cheng of Wu, Chen Tan of Yuzhang, and Chen Wenshao of Jiankang were examined, and their petitions proved true—his treacherous designs had accumulated over years.

sentences.zh: 昔周德初升，公旦有流言之釁，魯道方泰，季子斷逵泉之誅。

translations.literal: Formerly when Zhou's virtue first rose, the Duke of Zhou had the scandal of slanderous talk; when Lu's way was flourishing, the younger son cut off the execution at Kuiquan.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Zhou's virtue first rose, the Duke of Zhou faced slander; when Lu flourished, the younger son halted an execution at Kuiquan.

sentences.zh: 近則淮厲覆車於前，義康襲軌於後，變發柴奇，禍成范、謝，亦皆以義奪親，情為憲屈。

translations.literal: Recently the Prince of Huai overturned his carriage in front, Yikang followed the track behind; disaster arose with Chai Qi, calamity formed with Fan and Xie—they too all let righteousness overcome kinship, and feeling yielded to law.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Prince Huai's fate warned from the front and Yikang's from behind; disasters involving Chai Qi, Fan, and Xie all showed righteousness overcoming kinship and private feeling yielding to law.

sentences.zh: 況乃上悖天經，下誣政道，結釁於無妄之辰，希幸于文明之日，皇穹所不覆，厚土所不容。

translations.literal: How much more when one rebels against Heaven's constant above and deceives the way of government below, forging enmity in a time without cause, hoping for fortune in a day of civilization—August Heaven will not cover him, thick earth will not bear him.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when one rebels against Heaven above and corrupts government below, plotting treason in a time of peace and hoping for fortune in an age of civilization—Heaven will not shelter him, earth will not bear him.

sentences.zh: 夫無禮之誡，臣子所宜服膺；

translations.literal: The admonition against lack of ritual is what subjects and sons should take to heart;
translations.idiomatic: The warning against breach of ritual is what every subject should take to heart;

sentences.zh: 幹紀之刑，有國所應慎守。

translations.literal: the punishment for violating the statutes is what a state ought carefully to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: and the punishment for violating the statutes is what every state must uphold.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，宜下有司，絕誕屬籍，削爵土，收付延尉法獄治罪。

translations.literal: Your servants jointly propose that the relevant offices should be ordered to strike Dan from the clan registers, strip his rank and fief, seize him and deliver him to the Minister of Justice's penal prison for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly propose that the relevant offices strike Dan from the clan registers, strip his rank and fief, and deliver him to the Minister of Justice for trial and punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸所連坐，別下考論。

translations.literal: All those implicated by association should be separately ordered for investigation and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: All those implicated should be separately investigated and judged.

sentences.zh: 伏願遠尋宗周之重，近監興亡之由，割恩棄私，俯順群議，則卜世靈根，於茲克固，鴻勳盛烈，永永無窮。

translations.literal: We humbly wish that Your Majesty would look far back to the weight of the Zhou founders and examine near at hand the causes of rise and fall, cut off favor and abandon private feeling, bow to the collective counsel—then the divined age and spiritual root may here be made firm, and great merit and splendid achievement endure without end.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly pray that Your Majesty look back to the Zhou founders and the causes of rise and fall, set aside private favor, and heed our counsel—then the dynasty's foundation will be secured and its glory endure forever.

sentences.zh: 陛下如復隱忍，未垂三思，則覆皇基於七百，擠生民於塗炭。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty again shows forbearance and does not give threefold thought, you will overturn the imperial foundation of seven hundred years and drive the living people into charcoal and mud.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty again shows forbearance and does not reflect deeply, you will overturn the foundation of seven hundred years and drive the people into misery.

sentences.zh: 此臣等所以夙夜危懼，不敢避鈇鉞之誅者也。

translations.literal: This is why your servants day and night are in peril and fear, and dare not avoid execution by axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: This is why we lie awake in fear and dare not shrink from the axe, even at the cost of our lives.

sentences.zh: 上不許，有司又固請，乃貶爵為侯，遣令之國。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent; the offices again firmly petitioned, and he was only degraded in rank to marquis and ordered to go to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; when the offices petitioned again, Dan was only degraded to marquis and ordered to depart for his fief.

sentences.zh: 上將誅誕，以義興太守垣閬為兗州刺史，配以羽林禁兵，遣給事中戴明寶隨閬襲誕，使閬以之鎮為名。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to execute Dan; he made the Yixing governor Yuan Lang Governor of Yan, paired him with Forbidden Guards of the Forest, and sent the Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Dai Mingbao with Lang to strike Dan, having Lang go in the name of taking up his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to execute Dan. He appointed Yuan Lang, governor of Yixing, as governor of Yan, gave him Forbidden Guards, and sent Attendant Dai Mingbao with him to strike Dan under the pretext of taking up his post.

sentences.zh: 閬至廣陵，誕未悟也。

translations.literal: Lang reached Guangling; Dan had not yet understood.
translations.idiomatic: Lang reached Guangling, and Dan still did not suspect.

sentences.zh: 明寶夜報誕典籤蔣成，使明晨開門為內應。

translations.literal: Mingbao by night informed Dan's registrar Jiang Cheng to open the gate the next morning as inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Mingbao secretly informed Dan's registrar Jiang Cheng to open the gate the next morning as an inside collaborator.

sentences.zh: 成以告府舍人許宗之，宗之奔入告誕。

translations.literal: Cheng told the residence aide Xu Zongzhi; Zongzhi ran in to inform Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng told the residence aide Xu Zongzhi, who ran in to warn Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕驚起，呼左右及素所畜養數百人，執蔣成，勒兵自衛。

translations.literal: Dan started up in alarm, called his attendants and several hundred men he had long kept and trained, seized Jiang Cheng, and marshaled troops to defend himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dan started up in alarm, summoned his attendants and several hundred retainers he had long kept, seized Jiang Cheng, and marshaled troops to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 明旦將曉，明寶與閬率精兵數百人卒至，天明而門不開，誕已列兵登陴，自在門上斬蔣成，焚兵籍，赦作部徒系囚，開門遣腹心率壯士擊明寶等，破之。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, just before light, Mingbao and Lang led several hundred elite troops who suddenly arrived; when day broke the gate did not open. Dan had already drawn up troops on the ramparts, personally beheaded Jiang Cheng on the gate, burned the military registers, pardoned laborers and bound prisoners of the workshops, opened the gate and sent his intimates leading stalwart warriors to strike Mingbao and the others, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Mingbao and Lang arrived with several hundred elite troops, but the gate remained shut. Dan had drawn up his men on the walls, personally beheaded Jiang Cheng at the gate, burned the military registers, freed workshop prisoners, and sent his trusted warriors out to rout Mingbao's force.

sentences.zh: 閬即遇害，明寶奔逃，自海陵界得還。

translations.literal: Lang was immediately killed; Mingbao fled and escaped, returning from the Hailing border.
translations.idiomatic: Lang was killed on the spot; Mingbao fled and escaped back across the Hailing border.

sentences.zh: 上乃遣車騎大將軍沈慶之率大眾討誕。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent the General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi leading a great host to suppress Dan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi at the head of a great army to suppress Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕焚燒郭邑，驅居民百姓，悉使入城，分遣書檄，要結近遠。

translations.literal: Dan burned the outer city, drove the resident common people, and made them all enter the city; he sent out letters and proclamations in all directions to bind near and far by covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Dan burned the suburbs, drove all the residents into the city, and sent proclamations far and wide to rally supporters.

sentences.zh: 時山陽內史梁曠家在廣陵，誕執其妻子，遣使要曠，曠斬使拒之。

translations.literal: At the time the Shanyang Administrator Liang Kuang's family was in Guangling; Dan seized his wife and children and sent envoys to summon Kuang; Kuang beheaded the envoys and refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyang administrator Liang Kuang's family was in Guangling; Dan seized his wife and children and sent envoys to summon him, but Kuang beheaded the envoys and refused.

sentences.zh: 誕怒，滅其家。

translations.literal: Dan in anger exterminated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Dan in his rage exterminated the entire household.

sentences.zh: 誕奉表投之城外，曰：「往年元兇禍逆，陛下入討，臣背凶赴順，可謂常節。

translations.literal: Dan submitted a memorial cast outside the walls, saying: "In former years the usurper committed treacherous disaster; when Your Majesty marched to suppress him, your servant turned from the wicked to the righteous—this may be called ordinary duty.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent a memorial out beyond the walls, saying: "In former years, when the usurper committed his crimes, Your Majesty marched to suppress him, and I turned from the wicked to the righteous—that was only my proper duty.

sentences.zh: 及丞相構難，臧、魯協從，朝野恍惚，鹹懷憂懼，陛下欲百官羽儀，星馳推奉，臣前後固執。

translations.literal: When the Chancellor raised trouble and Zang and Lu joined in accord, court and countryside were dazed; all bore worry and fear. Your Majesty wished the hundred officials with imperial regalia to rush like stars in urging submission; your servant repeatedly held firm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chancellor raised rebellion and Zang and Lu joined him, court and countryside were in turmoil. Your Majesty wished to send the officials with imperial regalia to urge submission, but I repeatedly refused.

sentences.zh: 方賜允俞，社稷獲全，是誰之力？

translations.literal: Only then was consent granted and the altars of state preserved—whose power was this?
translations.idiomatic: Only then was consent granted and the altars of state preserved—whose doing was that?

sentences.zh: 陛下接遇殷勤，累加榮寵，驃騎、揚州，旬月移授，恩秩頻加，復賜徐、兗，仰屈皇儲，遠相餞送。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received and treated me with earnest kindness, repeatedly adding glory and favor—General of Agile Cavalry, Yangzhou, transferred within a month and a half, ranks of grace added again and again, then Xu and Yan bestowed, bending the imperial heir to send him far in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty treated me with earnest kindness, heaping honors upon me—General of Agile Cavalry, governor of Yangzhou, transferred within weeks, then Xu and Yan as well, even bending the heir apparent to send him far in farewell.

sentences.zh: 臣一遇之感，感此何忘，庶希偕老，永相娛慰。

translations.literal: Your servant, moved at a single meeting—how could I forget this feeling? I hoped to grow old together and forever share comfort and joy.
translations.idiomatic: I was moved by a single meeting—how could I forget? I hoped we would grow old together in mutual trust and joy.

sentences.zh: 豈謂陛下信用讒言，遂令無名小人來相掩襲，不任枉酷即加誅剪。

translations.literal: Who would have thought Your Majesty would trust slanderous words and send nameless petty men to make a surprise attack, unable to bear wrongful cruelty and at once add execution and cutting down?
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought Your Majesty would trust slander and send nameless petty men to attack me by surprise, unable to bear wrongful cruelty and at once order my execution?

sentences.zh: 雀鼠貪生，仰違詔敕。

translations.literal: Sparrow and rat cling to life; I have disobeyed the edict above.
translations.idiomatic: Like sparrow and rat I cling to life and have disobeyed your edict.

sentences.zh: 今親勒部曲，鎮捍徐、兗。

translations.literal: Now I personally lead my troops to garrison and defend Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Now I personally lead my troops to defend Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 先經何福，同生皇家；

translations.literal: What blessing did we share before, born of the same imperial house;
translations.idiomatic: What blessing did we once share, born of the same imperial house;

sentences.zh: 今有何愆，便成胡、越？

translations.literal: what fault do I have now that we have become Hu and Yue?
translations.idiomatic: what fault have I now that we have become strangers like Hu and Yue?

sentences.zh: 陵鋒奮戈，萬沒豈顧，蕩定以期，冀在旦夕。

translations.literal: I will charge the front and brandish weapons; though ten thousand perish I will not look back; pacification I expect, hoping it comes within days.
translations.idiomatic: I will charge the front and brandish my weapons; though ten thousand perish I will not look back; I expect pacification within days.

sentences.zh: 右軍、宣蘭，爰及武昌，皆以無罪，並遇枉酷，臣有何過，復致於此。

translations.literal: The Right Army, Xuanlan, and Wuchang as well—all without guilt, all met wrongful cruelty; what fault have I that I should come to this again?
translations.idiomatic: The Right Army, Xuanlan, and Wuchang—all innocent, all met wrongful cruelty; what fault have I that I should come to this again?

sentences.zh: 陛下宮帷之醜，豈可三緘。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's shame within the palace curtains—how can it be sealed thrice?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's shame within the palace curtains—how can it be sealed thrice over?

sentences.zh: 臨紙悲塞，不知所言。」

translations.literal: Facing the paper, grief chokes me; I know not what to say."
translations.idiomatic: Facing this paper, grief chokes me; I know not what more to say."

sentences.zh: 世祖忿誕，左右腹心同籍朞親並誅之，死者以千數。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was furious at Dan; his attendants, intimates, those of the same register and nearest kin were all executed—the dead numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was furious at Dan; his attendants, intimates, and nearest kin of the same register were all executed—the dead numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 或有家人已死，方自城內叛出者。

translations.literal: Some whose families had already been killed only then defected from within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Some whose families had already been killed only then defected from within the city.

sentences.zh: 車駕出頓宣武堂，內外纂嚴。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage went out and halted at the Hall of Martial Display; within and without, strict guard was drawn up.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went out and halted at the Hall of Martial Display; strict guard was drawn up throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 慶之進廣陵，誕幢主韓道元來降。

translations.literal: Qingzhi advanced on Guangling; Dan's banner commander Han Daoyuan came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi advanced on Guangling, and Dan's banner commander Han Daoyuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史宗愨、徐州刺史劉道隆率眾來會。

translations.literal: The Yu Governor Zong Que and the Xu Governor Liu Daolong led their hosts to join him.
translations.idiomatic: The governors of Yu and Xu, Zong Que and Liu Daolong, led their armies to join him.

sentences.zh: 誕中兵參軍柳光宗、參軍何康之、劉元邁、幢主索智朗謀開城北門歸順，未期而康之所鎮隊主石貝子先眾出奔，康之懼事泄，夜與智朗斬關而出。

translations.literal: Dan's Central Army Major Liu Guangzong, the aides He Kangzhi and Liu Yuanmai, and the banner commander Suo Zhilang plotted to open the north gate of the city and surrender; before the appointed time the squad leader Shi Beizi under Kangzhi's command fled ahead of the crowd; Kangzhi feared the affair would leak and by night with Zhilang cut the gate bars and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's staff officers Liu Guangzong, He Kangzhi, Liu Yuanmai, and banner commander Suo Zhilang plotted to open the north gate and surrender; before the appointed time Kangzhi's squad leader Shi Beizi fled ahead of the rest, and Kangzhi, fearing exposure, cut the gate bars by night and escaped with Zhilang.

sentences.zh: 誕禽光宗殺之。

translations.literal: Dan seized Guangzong and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan seized Guangzong and killed him.

sentences.zh: 光宗，柳元景從弟也。

translations.literal: Guangzong was the younger cousin of Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong was the younger cousin of Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 康之母在城內，亦為誕所殺。

translations.literal: Kangzhi's mother was within the city and was also killed by Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi's mother, who was still in the city, was also killed by Dan.

sentences.zh: 誕見眾軍大集，欲棄城北走，留中兵參軍申靈賜居守，自將騎步數百人，親信並隨，聲云出戰，邪趨海陵道。

translations.literal: Dan, seeing the massed armies gathering, wished to abandon the city and flee north; he left the Central Army Major Shen Lingci to hold and defend it, himself leading several hundred cavalry and infantry with his intimates following, claiming he was going out to battle but turning aside toward the Hailing road.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the armies massing, Dan planned to abandon the city and flee north. He left Shen Lingci to hold the city and himself led several hundred cavalry and infantry, claiming to go out to battle but turning toward the Hailing road.

sentences.zh: 誕將周豐生馳告慶之，慶之遣龍驤將軍武念追躡。

translations.literal: Dan's general Zhou Fengsheng galloped to inform Qingzhi; Qingzhi sent the Dragon-Charger General Wu Nian in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's general Zhou Fengsheng galloped to inform Qingzhi, who sent General Wu Nian in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 誕行十餘里，眾並不欲去，請誕還城。

translations.literal: Dan had gone more than ten li when the crowd all did not wish to leave and asked Dan to return to the city.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten li, his men all refused to go on and begged Dan to return to the city.

sentences.zh: 誕曰：「我還，卿能為我盡力不？」

translations.literal: Dan said: "If I return, can you all exert yourselves for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Dan said: "If I return, will you all fight for me with all your strength?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「願盡力。」

translations.literal: The crowd all said: "We wish to exert ourselves fully."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered: "We will fight with all our strength."

sentences.zh: 左右楊承伯牽誕馬曰：「死生且還保城，欲持此安之？

translations.literal: The attendant Yang Chengbo pulled Dan's horse and said: "Whether life or death, return and hold the city—where do you think to go with this?
translations.idiomatic: His attendant Yang Chengbo seized Dan's horse and said: "Whether we live or die, we must hold the city—where do you think you can go out here?

sentences.zh: 速還尚得入，不然，敗矣。」

translations.literal: Return quickly and you can still get in; otherwise, it is defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Return quickly and we can still get in; otherwise we are lost."

sentences.zh: 慶之所遣將戴寶之單騎前至，刺誕殆獲，誕懼，乃馳還。

translations.literal: The general Dai Baozhi whom Qingzhi had sent came alone on horseback ahead, stabbed at Dan and nearly seized him; Dan in fear galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Baozhi, whom Qingzhi had sent ahead, came alone on horseback and nearly struck Dan down; Dan in fear galloped back.

sentences.zh: 武念去誕遠，未及至，故誕得向城。

translations.literal: Wu Nian was far from Dan and had not yet arrived, so Dan was able to head for the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nian was still far behind and had not yet arrived, so Dan was able to reach the city.

sentences.zh: 既至，曰：「城上白鬚，非沈公邪？」

translations.literal: When he arrived he said: "The white beard on the wall—is that not Master Shen?"
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he said: "The white beard on the wall—is that not Master Shen?"

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「申中兵。」

translations.literal: His attendants said: "Central Army Major Shen."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said: "Central Army Major Shen."

sentences.zh: 誕乃入。

translations.literal: Dan then entered.
translations.idiomatic: Dan then entered the city.

sentences.zh: 以靈賜為驃騎府錄事參軍，王璵之為中軍長史，世子景粹為中軍將軍，州別駕范義為中軍長史，其餘府州文武，皆加秩。

translations.literal: He made Lingci Recorder of the Agile Cavalry Headquarters, Wang Yuzhi Central Army Senior Aide, the heir Jingcui Central Army General, the provincial aide Fan Yi Central Army Senior Aide; all other civil and military officers of the administration and province received raised rank.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Lingci recorder of the Agile Cavalry headquarters, Wang Yuzhi senior aide of the central army, his heir Jingcui central army general, and Fan Yi senior aide of the central army; all other civil and military officers received promotions.

sentences.zh: 先是，右衛將軍垣護之、左軍將軍崔道固、屯騎校尉龐番虯、太子旅賁中郎將殷孝祖破索虜還，至廣陵，上並使受慶之節度。

translations.literal: Earlier, the General of the Right Guard Yuan Huzhi, the General of the Left Army Cui Daogu, the Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Pang Fanqiu, and the Palace Guard Major of the Heir Apparent Yin Xiaozu, having defeated the northern barbarians, returned and reached Guangling; the emperor had them all placed under Qingzhi's command.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Generals Yuan Huzhi, Cui Daogu, Colonel Pang Fanqiu, and Major Yin Xiaozu, having defeated the northern barbarians, reached Guangling, and the emperor placed them all under Qingzhi's command.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史劉季之，誕故佐也，驍果有膂力，梁山之役，又有戰功，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: The Si Governor Liu Jizhi was a former aide of Dan's, bold and strong in physique; in the Liangshan campaign he again had battle merit and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Si, Liu Jizhi, had been Dan's former aide, bold and powerful; at Liangshan he won merit again and his fief was increased by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 在州貪殘，司馬翟弘業諫爭甚苦，季之積忿，置毒藥食中殺之。

translations.literal: In the province he was greedy and cruel; the Administrator Zhai Hongye remonstrated with great pain; Jizhi nursed resentment and put poison in food to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he was greedy and cruel; his administrator Zhai Hongye remonstrated bitterly, and Jizhi in resentment poisoned his food and killed him.

sentences.zh: 少年時，宗愨共蒱戲，曾手侮加愨，愨深銜恨。

translations.literal: In youth he had played dice with Zong Que and once with his hand insulted and struck Que; Que deeply bore hatred.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had played dice with Zong Que and once struck him with his hand; Que bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 至是愨為豫州刺史，都督司州，季之慮愨為禍，乃委官間道欲歸朝廷。

translations.literal: By this time Que was Governor of Yu and Commander of Si; Jizhi feared Que would bring disaster and resigned his office, taking secret paths wishing to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: By then Que was governor of Yu and commander of Si; Jizhi feared Que would harm him, resigned his office, and tried to return to court by secret paths.

sentences.zh: 會誕反，季之至盱眙，盱眙太守鄭瑗以季之素為誕所遇，疑其同逆，因邀道殺之，送首詣道隆。

translations.literal: It happened that Dan rebelled; Jizhi reached Xuyi; the Xuyi governor Zheng Yuan, because Jizhi had long been favored by Dan, suspected him of joining the rebellion and invited him on the road and killed him, sending the head to Daolong.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan rebelled, Jizhi reached Xuyi; the governor Zheng Yuan, knowing Jizhi had long served Dan, suspected him of joining the rebellion, ambushed and killed him on the road, and sent his head to Daolong.

sentences.zh: 時誕亦遣間信要季之，及季之首至，沈慶之送以示誕。

translations.literal: At the time Dan had also sent a secret message summoning Jizhi; when Jizhi's head arrived, Shen Qingzhi sent it to show Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had also sent a secret summons to Jizhi; when Jizhi's head arrived, Shen Qingzhi sent it to show Dan.

sentences.zh: 季之缺齒，垣護之亦缺，誕謂眾曰：「此垣護之頭，非劉季之也。」

translations.literal: Jizhi lacked teeth; Yuan Huzhi also lacked teeth; Dan said to the crowd: "This is Yuan Huzhi's head, not Liu Jizhi's."
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi was missing teeth, and Yuan Huzhi was too; Dan told the crowd: "This is Yuan Huzhi's head, not Liu Jizhi's."

sentences.zh: 誕幢主公孫安期率兵隊出降。

translations.literal: Dan's banner commander Gongsun Anqi led his troop out in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's banner commander Gongsun Anqi led his troop out in surrender.

sentences.zh: 誕初閉城拒使，記室參軍賀弼固諫再三，誕怒，抽刃向之，乃止。

translations.literal: When Dan first closed the city and refused the envoys, the Recorder He Bi firmly remonstrated again and again; Dan in anger drew his blade toward him, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan first closed the city and refused the envoys, his recorder He Bi remonstrated again and again; Dan in anger drew his blade toward him, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 或勸弼出降，弼曰：「公舉兵向朝廷，此事既不可從；

translations.literal: Some urged Bi to go out and surrender; Bi said: "The lord has raised troops against the court—this matter I cannot follow;
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Bi to surrender; Bi said: "My lord has raised troops against the court—that I cannot follow;

sentences.zh: 荷公厚恩，又義無違背，唯當死明心耳。」

translations.literal: I have received the lord's deep grace, and in righteousness there is no betrayal—I can only die to make my heart clear."
translations.idiomatic: yet I have received his deep grace, and in righteousness I cannot betray him—I can only die to prove my loyalty."

sentences.zh: 乃服藥自殺。

translations.literal: He then took poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then took poison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 弼字仲輔，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Bi, styled Zhongfu, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, whose courtesy name was Zhongfu, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 有文才。

translations.literal: He had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、山陽、海陵二郡太守，長史如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of the two commanderies of Shanyang and Hailing, Senior Aide as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of Chariots and Cavalry and governor of Shanyang and Hailing, with his former rank as senior aide.

sentences.zh: 幢主王璵之賞募數百人，從東門出攻龍驤將軍程天祚營，斷其弩弦，天祚擊破之，即走還城。

translations.literal: The banner commander Wang Yuzhi rewarded and recruited several hundred men, went out from the east gate to attack the Dragon-Charger General Cheng Tianzuo's camp, cut his crossbow strings; Tianzuo struck and defeated them, and they at once fled back to the city.
translations.idiomatic: Banner commander Wang Yuzhi recruited several hundred men, went out the east gate to attack General Cheng Tianzuo's camp, and cut his crossbow strings; Tianzuo routed them and they fled back into the city.

sentences.zh: 誕又加申靈賜南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Dan again promoted Shen Lingci to Governor of Southern Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Dan again promoted Shen Lingci to governor of Southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 軍主馬元子踰城歸順，追及殺之，乃於城內建列立壇誓，誕將歃血，其所署輔國將軍孟玉秀曰：「陛下親歃。」

translations.literal: The army commander Ma Yuanzi climbed over the wall to surrender; pursued and killed. Then within the city they set ranks and erected an altar for oath; Dan was about to drink the blood oath when his appointed General Who Supports the State Meng Yuxiu said: "Your Majesty should drink in person."
translations.idiomatic: Army commander Ma Yuanzi climbed over the wall to surrender but was pursued and killed. Within the city they set ranks and erected an altar for oath; as Dan was about to drink the blood oath, his appointed General Meng Yuxiu said: "Your Majesty should drink in person."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The assembled ministers all cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers all cried "Long live the Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 初，誕使黃門呂曇濟與左右素所信者，將世子景粹藏於民間，謂曰：「事若濟，斯命全脫，如其不免，可深埋之。」

translations.literal: Earlier Dan had sent the Yellow Gate Lü Tanji with those among his attendants he had long trusted to hide the heir Jingcui among the common people, saying: "If the affair succeeds, this life may be wholly preserved; if it cannot be avoided, you may bury him deep.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dan had sent the Yellow Gate Lü Tanji with trusted attendants to hide his heir Jingcui among the common people, saying: "If we succeed, he may be saved; if not, bury him deep.

sentences.zh: 分以金寶，齊送出門，並各散走。

translations.literal: He divided gold and jewels among them, all escorted out the gate, and each scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He divided gold and jewels among them, sent them all out the gate, and each scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 唯曇濟不去，攜負景粹，十餘日，乃為沈慶之所捕得，斬之。

translations.literal: Only Tanji did not leave; carrying Jingcui on his back, after more than ten days he was captured by Shen Qingzhi and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tanji did not leave; carrying Jingcui on his back, after more than ten days he was captured by Shen Qingzhi and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 誕所署平南將軍虞季充又出降書。

translations.literal: Dan's appointed General Who Pacifies the South Yu Jichong again sent out a letter of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Yu Jichong, again sent out a letter of surrender.

sentences.zh: 上使慶之於桑里置烽火三所。

translations.literal: The emperor had Qingzhi set up three beacon-fire stations at Sangli.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Qingzhi set up three beacon-fire stations at Sangli.

sentences.zh: 誕又遣千餘人自北門攻強弩將軍苟思達營，龍驤將軍宗越擊破之。

translations.literal: Dan again sent more than a thousand men from the north gate to attack the Strong Crossbow General Gou Sida's camp; the Dragon-Charger General Zong Yue struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan again sent more than a thousand men from the north gate to attack General Gou Sida's camp; General Zong Yue routed them.

sentences.zh: 開東門掩攻劉道隆營，復為殷孝祖及員外散騎侍郎沈攸之所破。

translations.literal: They opened the east gate and made a surprise attack on Liu Daolong's camp, but were again defeated by Yin Xiaozu and the Extraordinary Cadet Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the east gate for a surprise assault on Liu Daolong's camp but were again routed by Yin Xiaozu and Shen Youzhi, Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 誕又加申靈賜左長史，王璵之右長史，范義左司馬、左將軍，孟玉秀右司馬、右將軍。

translations.literal: Dan further appointed Shen Lingci Left Senior Aide, Wang Yuzhi Right Senior Aide, Fan Yi Left Staff Major and Left General, and Meng Yuxiu Right Staff Major and Right General.
translations.idiomatic: Dan further promoted Shen Lingci to left senior aide, Wang Yuzhi to right senior aide, Fan Yi to left staff major and left general, and Meng Yuxiu to right staff major and right general.

sentences.zh: 范義母妻子並在城內，有勸義出降，義曰：「我人吏也，且豈能作何康活邪！」

translations.literal: Fan Yi's mother, wife, and children were all inside the city; some urged Yi to go out and surrender. Yi said, "I am his subordinate officer—how could I play the He Kang and survive!
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yi's mother, wife, and children were all in the city, and some urged him to surrender. He said, "I am Dan's man—how could I pull a He Kang and live through it!

sentences.zh: 義字明休，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Mingxiu, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, whose courtesy name was Mingxiu, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 早有世譽。

translations.literal: From early on he enjoyed repute in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had enjoyed a fine reputation from early on.

sentences.zh: 五月十九日夜，有流星大如斗杆，尾長十餘丈，從西北來墜城內，是謂天狗。

translations.literal: On the night of the nineteenth day of the fifth month, a meteor as large as a dipper-pole, its tail more than ten zhang long, came from the northwest and fell inside the city—this is called the Celestial Dog.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the nineteenth of the fifth month a meteor as large as a dipper handle, its tail more than ten zhang long, fell from the northwest into the city—the Celestial Dog.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天狗所墜，下有伏尸流血。」

translations.literal: Prognostication says: "Where the Celestial Dog falls, below there are hidden corpses and flowing blood.
translations.idiomatic: Omens read: "Where the Celestial Dog falls, corpses lie hidden below and blood runs.

sentences.zh: 誕又遣二百人出東門攻劉道產營，別遣疑兵二百人出北門。

translations.literal: Dan again sent two hundred men out the east gate to attack Liu Daochan's camp, and separately sent two hundred decoy troops out the north gate.
