translations.idiomatic: Dan again sent two hundred men out the east gate against Liu Daochan's camp while dispatching two hundred decoy troops from the north gate.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之於東門奮短兵接戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi at the east gate wielded short weapons and joined battle, greatly defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi fought hand to hand at the east gate and routed them.

sentences.zh: 門者又為苟思達所破。

translations.literal: The gate attackers were again defeated by Gou Sida.
translations.idiomatic: The attackers at the gate were beaten again by Gou Sida.

sentences.zh: 誕又遣數百人出東門攻寧朔司馬劉勔營，攸之又破之。

translations.literal: Dan again sent several hundred men out the east gate to attack the Pacifier of the North Staff Major Liu Mian's camp; Youzhi again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent several hundred more out the east gate against Staff Major Liu Mian's camp; Youzhi routed them again.

sentences.zh: 廣陵城舊不開南門，云開南門者，不利其主，至誕乃開焉。

translations.literal: Guangling city in the past did not open its south gate; it was said that opening the south gate was unlucky for its ruler—only with Dan was it opened.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling had never opened its south gate; tradition held that doing so boded ill for the city's master—Dan was the first to open it.

sentences.zh: 彭城邵領宗在城內，陰結死士，欲襲誕。

translations.literal: Shao Lingzong of Pengcheng was inside the city, secretly gathering determined men, intending to strike at Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Lingzong of Pengcheng, inside the city, secretly assembled men willing to die in order to assassinate Dan.

sentences.zh: 先欲布誠於慶之，乃說誕求為間諜，見許。

translations.literal: First wishing to declare his sincerity to Qingzhi, he persuaded Dan to ask to serve as a spy, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He first wanted to pledge loyalty to Qingzhi, so he persuaded Dan to let him serve as a spy, and Dan agreed.

sentences.zh: 領宗既出，致誠畢，復還城內，事泄，誕鞭二百，考問不服，遂支解之。

translations.literal: Lingzong once out, having finished declaring his sincerity, returned inside the city; the affair leaked out; Dan had him flogged two hundred strokes, interrogated him—he would not confess—and finally had him torn limb from limb.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving to signal his loyalty to Qingzhi, Lingzong returned inside the city; when the plot was exposed Dan had him flogged two hundred times and tortured him, but he would not confess, so Dan had him dismembered.

sentences.zh: 上遣送章二紐，其一曰竟陵縣開國侯，食邑一千戶，募賞禽誕；

translations.literal: The emperor sent two pairs of seals: the first read Marquis Who Establishes the State of Jingling County, fief of one thousand households, with a bounty for capturing Dan alive;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent two seal cords: one conferring Marquis Who Establishes the State of Jingling County with a fief of one thousand households and a bounty for capturing Dan alive;

sentences.zh: 其二曰建興縣開國男，三百戶，募賞先登。

translations.literal: the second read Baron Who Establishes the State of Jianxing County, three hundred households, with a bounty for being first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: the other conferring Baron Who Establishes the State of Jianxing County with three hundred households and a bounty for the first man over the wall.

sentences.zh: 若克外城，舉一烽；

translations.literal: If the outer wall was taken, raise one beacon;
translations.idiomatic: Capture of the outer wall: one beacon.

sentences.zh: 克內城，舉兩烽；

translations.literal: if the inner wall was taken, raise two beacons;
translations.idiomatic: If the inner wall was taken, raise two beacons;

sentences.zh: 禽誕，舉三烽。

translations.literal: if Dan was captured alive, raise three beacons.
translations.idiomatic: If Dan was captured alive, raise three beacons.

sentences.zh: 上又遣屯騎校尉譚金、前虎賁中郎將鄭景玄率羽林兵隸慶之。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent Commandant of Escort Cavalry Tan Jin and former Tiger-Fierce Captain General Zheng Jingxuan leading Forest Guard troops to serve under Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also dispatched Tan Jin, Commandant of Escort Cavalry, and former Tiger-Fierce Captain General Zheng Jingxuan with Forest Guard troops to serve under Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 誕復遣三百人自南門攻劉勔土山，為勔所破。

translations.literal: Dan again sent three hundred men from the south gate to attack Liu Mian's earthen mound, and was defeated by Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Dan sent three hundred men from the south gate against Liu Mian's siege mound; Mian repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 慶之填塹治攻道，值夏雨，不得攻城。

translations.literal: Qingzhi filled moats and prepared assault routes, but encountered summer rains and could not attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi filled the moats and built assault paths, but summer rains prevented a siege.

sentences.zh: 上每璽書催督之，前後相繼。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent imperial-seal letters to press and supervise him; they followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a steady stream of imperial letters pressing him to attack.

sentences.zh: 及晴，再怒，使太史擇發日，將自濟江。

translations.literal: When it cleared, anger again, he had the Grand Astrologer choose a day of departure and was about to cross the river himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the weather cleared he grew angry once more, had the Grand Astrologer fix a day of departure, and prepared to cross the Yangtze himself.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭上表諫曰：「誕素無才略，畜養又寡，自拒王命，士庶離散。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince of Jiangxia Yigong submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Dan has never had talent or strategy, and his nurture of followers is meager; since he defied the imperial command, officers and commoners have scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, memorialized in protest: "Dan has never shown talent or strategy and commands few loyal followers; ever since he defied the throne, his soldiers and people have been melting away.

sentences.zh: 城內乏糧，器械不足，徒賴免兵倉頭三四百人，造次相附，恩怨夙結。

translations.literal: Inside the city grain is scarce and weapons insufficient; he relies solely on three or four hundred conscript soldiers and granary clerks hastily attached to him, old grudges and favors long entangled.
translations.idiomatic: The city lacks grain and arms; he depends on a hastily gathered band of three or four hundred conscript soldiers and clerks, bound by old loves and hatreds.

sentences.zh: 臣始短慮，謂一旬可殄，而假息流遷，七十餘日。

translations.literal: I at first thought narrowly that he could be extinguished in ten days, yet respite drags on—more than seventy days already.
translations.idiomatic: I originally hoped he could be crushed within ten days, yet more than seventy days have passed while he lingers on.

sentences.zh: 上將受律，群蕃嶽峙，銳卒精旅，動以萬計，大威所震，未有成功。

translations.literal: The sovereign is about to take command; feudal lords stand like mountain peaks; sharp soldiers and elite brigades, tens of thousands at a move—the full might shaken forth—yet success is still not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is ready to take the field; the princes stand massed like peaks; elite troops number in the tens of thousands—yet under all this imperial might there is still no victory.

sentences.zh: 臣雖凡怯，猶懷憤踴。

translations.literal: Though I am common and timid, I yet harbor indignant fervor.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and timid though I am, I burn with frustrated zeal.

sentences.zh: 陛下入翦封豕，出討長蛇，兵不血刃，再興七百。

translations.literal: Your Majesty entered to cut down the great boar, went out to chastise the long serpent; the army did not stain its blades, and the seven hundred years were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has cut down monstrous foes without staining a blade and restored the dynasty's glory—

sentences.zh: 而蕞爾小丑，遂延晷漏，致皇赫斯怒，將動乘輿。

translations.literal: yet this tiny clown has prolonged the turning of the sundial, stirring the August One's blazing wrath and moving the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: yet this wretched rebel has dragged out the siege until Your Sacred Majesty's wrath is aroused and the imperial carriage must stir.

sentences.zh: 此實臣下素食駑鈍之責，行留百司，莫不仰慚俯愧。

translations.literal: This is truly the fault of us subordinates who eat our salaries in idleness, dull and slow—every office at court and in the provinces, none but feels shame looking up and guilt looking down.
translations.idiomatic: This is our fault—idle, sluggish officials eating the state's bread—every office near and far hangs its head in shame.

sentences.zh: 今盛暑被甲，日費千金，天威一麾，孰不幸甚。

translations.literal: Now in sweltering heat men wear armor; a thousand gold is spent daily; at one wave of Heaven's majesty, who would not consider it the greater misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Armies stand in scorching heat in full armor; a thousand gold vanishes each day—and if Heaven's wrath stirs at one gesture, who would not suffer the more for it?

sentences.zh: 臣伏尋晉文王征淮南，淹師出二百日，方能制寇。

translations.literal: I respectfully recall that when Jin's Wen Wang campaigned against Huainan, he kept the army out two hundred days before he could subdue the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that when Emperor Wen of Jin campaigned against Huainan, the army was in the field two hundred days before the enemy was subdued.

sentences.zh: 今誕餱糧垂竭，背逆者多；

translations.literal: Now Dan's rations are nearly exhausted and many turn against him;
translations.idiomatic: Dan's provisions are almost gone and defections multiply;

sentences.zh: 慶之等轉悟遲重之非，漸見乘機之利。

translations.literal: Qingzhi and the others are coming to see the error of delay and heaviness, and gradually perceive the advantage of seizing the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi and his officers are waking to the cost of delay and beginning to see their opening.

sentences.zh: 且成旨頻降，必應旦夕夷殄。

translations.literal: Moreover, accomplished decrees descend repeatedly—surely within days he will be annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: And with Your Majesty's repeated orders, he should be wiped out within days.

sentences.zh: 愚又以廣陵塗近，人信易達，雖為江水，約示不難。

translations.literal: I further think that Guangling's road is near and word travels easily; though the Yangtze lies between, a pledge by edict would not be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling lies close at hand and news travels quickly; though the Yangtze intervenes, an edict of reassurance would not be hard to send.

sentences.zh: 且睹理者寡，暗塞者眾，忽見雲旗移次，京都既當祗悚，四方之志，必有未達。

translations.literal: Moreover, few see reason and many are blind and blocked; suddenly seeing the cloud-banner army shift its encampment, the capital will surely feel dread, and the mind of the four quarters will inevitably fail to understand.
translations.idiomatic: Few men grasp the logic, and many are closed-minded; a sudden shift of the imperial banners will frighten the capital and leave the realm puzzled.

sentences.zh: 臣愚伏重思計，今寧不當計小丑，省生命，以安遐邇之情。

translations.literal: I, in my foolishness, have bowed my head and thought again: would it not be better now to disregard this petty rebel, spare lives, and settle the feelings of near and far?
translations.idiomatic: On second thought, would it not be wiser to ignore this petty rebel, spare lives, and calm anxieties across the empire?

sentences.zh: 又以長江險闊，風波難期，王者尚不乘危，況乃泛不測之水。

translations.literal: Also, the Yangtze is perilously broad, wind and waves unpredictable—even kings do not court danger, how much less ride untried waters.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze is wide and treacherous, its storms unpredictable—a true king does not court danger, still less cross waters whose hazards cannot be known.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文濟江，遂有遺州之名，今雖先天不違，動干休慶，龍舟所幸，理必利涉，然居安慮危，不可不懼。

translations.literal: In olden days Emperor Wen of Wei crossed the river and thereafter bore the name of a state left behind; now though Heaven's prior approval is not violated, action touches blessed fortune, and where the dragon boat goes passage should by principle be fortunate—yet in security one must plan for peril; one cannot but fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Wei crossed the Yangtze his abandoned boat gave rise to the name of Yizhou; though Heaven smiles on Your Majesty and the dragon barge should pass safely, security demands foresight of danger—we cannot be heedless.

sentences.zh: 私誠款款，冒啟赤心，追用悚汗，不自宣盡。」

translations.literal: In private sincerity earnest and full, I venture to lay bare my loyal heart; thinking back I break into fearful sweat, and cannot express it all."
translations.idiomatic: With all my private sincerity I dare lay my heart before you; I tremble even to speak, and cannot say all I feel."

sentences.zh: 七月二日，慶之率眾軍進攻，克其外城，乘勝而進，又克小城。

translations.literal: On the second day of the seventh month, Qingzhi led the massed armies in assault, took the outer wall, pressed the victory and advanced, and took the inner wall as well.
translations.idiomatic: On the second of the seventh month Qingzhi led the combined armies in assault, stormed the outer wall, pressed forward, and took the inner citadel as well.

sentences.zh: 誕聞軍入，與申靈賜走趨後園。

translations.literal: Dan heard the army enter and fled with Shen Lingci toward the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan heard the enemy had broken in, he fled with Shen Lingci toward the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 隊主沈胤之、義征客周滿、胡思祖馳至，誕執玉鐶刀與左右數人散走，胤之等追及誕於橋上，誕舉刀自衛，胤之傷誕面，因墜水，引出殺之，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: Squad leader Shen Yin zhi, volunteer retainer Zhou Man, and Hu Sizu galloped up; Dan grasped a jade-ringed knife and scattered in flight with several attendants; Yin zhi and the others caught Dan on a bridge; Dan raised his knife to defend himself; Yin zhi wounded Dan's face; he thereupon fell into the water; they pulled him out and killed him, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leader Shen Yin zhi, volunteer Zhou Man, and Hu Sizu raced after him. Dan seized a jade-hilted knife and fled with a few attendants; they caught him on a bridge. He fought back and Yin zhi cut his face; he fell into the water, was dragged out and killed, and his head was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時年二十七，因葬廣陵，貶姓留氏。

translations.literal: He was twenty-seven; he was buried at Guangling and his clan was degraded to the surname Liu (meaning "detained").
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-seven; he was buried at Guangling and his clan was degraded to the surname Liu (meaning "detained").

sentences.zh: 同黨悉誅，殺城內男為京觀，死者數千，女口為軍賞。

translations.literal: All co-conspirators were executed; males in the city were killed to make a victory mound; the dead numbered several thousand; women were distributed as military reward.
translations.idiomatic: All his cohort were put to death; the men of the city were slaughtered and piled into a victory mound, several thousand dead; the women were given out as spoils to the troops.

sentences.zh: 誕母殷、妻徐，並自殺。

translations.literal: Dan's mother Yin and his wife Xu both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's mother, Lady Yin, and his wife, Lady Xu, both took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 追贈殷長寧園淑妃。

translations.literal: Lady Yin was posthumously given the title Shufei of Changning Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin was posthumously honored as Shufei of Changning Garden.

sentences.zh: 嘉梁曠誠節，擢為後將軍。

translations.literal: For his honest integrity Jia Liang was promoted to Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Liang was promoted to Rear General for his steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 封周滿山陽縣侯，食邑四百五十戶，胤之萊陽子，食邑三百五十戶。

translations.literal: Zhou Man was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanyang County with a fief of four hundred fifty households; Yin zhi as Viscount of Laiyang with three hundred fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Man was made Marquis of Shanyang with a fief of 450 households; Yin zhi was made Viscount of Laiyang with 350 households.

sentences.zh: 胡思祖高平縣男食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Hu Sizu was made Baron of Gaoping County with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sizu was made Baron of Gaoping with a fief of 200 households.

sentences.zh: 臨川內羊璿之以先協附誕，伏誅。

translations.literal: Yang Suanzhi, Interior Secretary of Linchuan, for having early on conspired and joined Dan, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Suanzhi, Interior Secretary of Linchuan, was put to death for having sided with Dan from the start.

sentences.zh: 誕為南徐州刺史，在京，夜大風飛落屋瓦，城門鹿床倒覆，誕心惡之。

translations.literal: When Dan was Governor of Southern Xuzhou and was at the capital, at night a great wind blew roof tiles flying and the deer-bed at the city gate toppled over; Dan's heart was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: While Dan served as governor of Southern Xuzhou in the capital, a night gale tore off roof tiles and overturned the gate barrier; he took it as a bad omen.

sentences.zh: 及遷鎮廣陵，入城，沖風暴起揚塵，晝晦。

translations.literal: When he moved to garrison Guangling and entered the city, a sudden windstorm arose and raised dust; day turned dark.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up his post at Guangling and entered the city, a sudden sandstorm blotted out the daylight.

sentences.zh: 又中夜閑坐，有赤光照室，見者莫不怪愕。

translations.literal: Again, sitting at leisure in the middle of the night, red light filled the chamber; all who saw it were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Once at midnight as he sat idle, a red glow filled the room, and all who saw it were terrified.

sentences.zh: 左右侍直，眠中夢人告之曰：「官鬚髮為矟毦。」

translations.literal: Attendants on duty dreamed in sleep that someone told them: "The lord's beard and hair have become spear-tassel fluff.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants dreamed that a voice said, "My lord's beard and hair have turned to spear tassels.

sentences.zh: 既覺，已失髻矣，如此者數十人，誕甚怪懼。

translations.literal: When they awoke, their topknots were already gone—this happened to several dozen men; Dan was greatly frightened and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When they woke their topknots were gone; this happened to dozens of men, and Dan was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，發民築治廣陵城，誕循行，有人干輿揚聲大罵曰：「大兵尋至，何以辛苦百姓！」

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming the people were conscripted to build and repair Guangling city; Dan made the rounds, and someone stepped before his carriage and shouted abuse: "Great armies will soon arrive—why torment the people!
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming, when Dan conscripted the people to rebuild Guangling's walls, a man stepped in front of his carriage and shouted, "The imperial host is nearly here—why torment the common folk!

sentences.zh: 誕執之，問其本末，答曰：「姓夷名孫，家在海陵。

translations.literal: Dan seized him and asked the whole story; he answered: "My surname is Yi and my given name is Sun; my home is in Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had him seized and questioned; he answered, "My surname is Yi, my name Sun; I live in Hailing.

sentences.zh: 天公去年與道佛共議，欲除此間民人，道佛苦諫得止。

translations.literal: Last year the Lord of Heaven conferred with Dafo and planned to wipe out the people here; Dafo remonstrated bitterly and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the Lord of Heaven and Dafo debated destroying all the people here, but Dafo pleaded until the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 大禍將至，何不立六慎門。」

translations.literal: Great calamity is about to come—why not establish the Gate of Six Cautions?
translations.idiomatic: Great catastrophe is coming—why not build the Gate of Six Cautions?

sentences.zh: 誕問：「六慎門云何？」

translations.literal: Dan asked: "What is the Gate of Six Cautions?
translations.idiomatic: Dan asked, "What is the Gate of Six Cautions?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「古時有言，禍不入六慎門。」

translations.literal: He answered: "There is an old saying: calamity does not enter the Gate of Six Cautions.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "There is an old saying: disaster does not pass the Gate of Six Cautions.

sentences.zh: 誕以其言狂悖，殺之。

translations.literal: Dan, because his words were mad and perverse, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had him executed for his insane talk.

sentences.zh: 又五音士忽狂易見鬼，驚怖啼哭曰：「外軍圍城，城上張白布帆。」

translations.literal: Again, a Music Master suddenly went mad, saw ghosts, and cried in terror: "Outside armies besiege the city; white cloth sails hang on the walls!
translations.idiomatic: A musician suddenly went mad, claimed to see ghosts, and wailed, "Enemy armies surround the city—white sailcloth hangs from the battlements!

sentences.zh: 誕執錄二十餘日，乃赦之。

translations.literal: Dan detained and recorded him for more than twenty days, then pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan held him for more than twenty days, then released him.

sentences.zh: 城陷之日，雲霧晦暝，白虹臨北門，亙屬城內。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell, clouds and mist were murky and dim; a white rainbow reached over the north gate and stretched connected into the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the city fell, murky clouds blotted out the sky and a white rainbow spanned from the north gate deep into the city.

sentences.zh: 八年，前廢帝即位，義陽王昶為征北將軍、徐州刺史，道經廣陵，上表曰：「竊聞淮南中霧，眷求遺緒；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, after the Deposed Former Emperor took the throne, Prince of Yiyang Chang, as General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Xuzhou, passed Guangling on his way and submitted a memorial: "I have heard how amid the mists of Huainan one cherishes what was left behind;
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, after the Deposed Emperor's successor took the throne, Prince Chang of Yiyang, en route as General Who Campaigns North and governor of Xuzhou, memorialized from Guangling: "I hear how after the fog over Huainan, posterity still cherishes what was lost;

sentences.zh: 楚英流殛，愛存丘墓。

translations.literal: when Chu Ying was cast out and put to death, affection preserved his mound and tomb.
translations.idiomatic: when Chu Ying was exiled and executed, love still kept his grave in mind.

sentences.zh: 並難結兩臣，義開二主，法雖事斷，禮或情申。

translations.literal: Both were hard bonds between two ministers, righteousness opening two sovereigns; though law by the matter was cut off, ritual sometimes let feeling speak.
translations.idiomatic: In both cases loyalty bound subject to two rulers, and though law severed the tie when the matter ended, rites could still give feeling its voice.

sentences.zh: 伏見故賊劉誕，稱戈犯節，自貽逆命，膏斧嬰戮，在憲已彰。

translations.literal: I humbly see the former rebel Liu Dan, who raised weapons against his station, brought rebellion upon himself, and met the gleaming axe and infant slaughter—the punishment of law is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant observes that the former rebel Liu Dan, who took up arms in breach of duty and brought execution on himself, has already paid the full penalty the law requires.

sentences.zh: 但尋屬忝皇枝，位叨列辟，一以罪終，魂骸莫赦。

translations.literal: Yet tracing his lineage he was born to the imperial branch and held rank among the feudal lords; once crime ended all, neither soul nor bones were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was of the imperial clan and held princely rank—once his crime was sealed, neither soul nor body received mercy.

sentences.zh: 生均宗籍，死同匹豎，旅窆委雜，封樹不修。

translations.literal: In life he shared the clan register; in death he equals a common fellow; the wandering burial is piled in disorder; the mound trees are unkept.
translations.idiomatic: In life he shared the imperial genealogy; in death he lies like any commoner, his coffin cast aside in neglect, his grave mound untended.

sentences.zh: 今歲月愈邁，愆流釁往，踐境興懷，感事傷目。

translations.literal: Now as months and years advance further, old offenses and wrongs flow away; treading this territory my heart rises, moved by events that wound the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Years have passed and old guilt has faded; yet treading this soil moves me, and the sight grieves me.

sentences.zh: 陛下繼明升運，鹹與惟新，大德方臨，哀矜未及。

translations.literal: Your Majesty succeeding the bright ascent of fortune, all things are made new together; great virtue has just arrived, and pity has not yet reached him.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited a bright new reign and renewed all things; your great virtue is still new, and compassion has not yet reached him.

sentences.zh: 夫欒布哭市，義犯雷霆；

translations.literal: Luan Bu weeping in the marketplace, righteousness braving the thunder;
translations.idiomatic: Luan Bu wept for Ji in the marketplace, defying imperial wrath;

sentences.zh: 田叔鉗赭，志於夷戮。

translations.literal: Tian Shu in chains and cangue, intent on execution by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Shu submitted himself in fetters, seeking to share his master's execution.

sentences.zh: 況在天倫，何獨無感。

translations.literal: How much more within the bonds of Heaven's kinship—why alone be without feeling?
translations.idiomatic: How much more within the bonds of kin—can Your Majesty alone remain unmoved?

sentences.zh: 伏願稽若前准，降申丹志，乞薄改褊祔，微表窀穸。

translations.literal: I humbly wish You would examine the former precedents, extend your crimson heart, and grant a modest change to partial ancestral enshrinement and a slight marking of the burial plot.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to follow those precedents, show a little mercy, and grant a modest re-inclusion in the ancestral rites and a simple marking of his tomb.

sentences.zh: 則朽骨知榮，窮泉識荷。

translations.literal: Then the rotten bones would know honor and the deep spring would know gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Then his bones in the grave would know honor, and his spirit below would feel your grace.

sentences.zh: 臨紙哽慟，辭不自宣。」

translations.literal: Facing the paper I choke with grief; the words cannot declare themselves.
translations.idiomatic: My grief chokes me as I write; words fail to say what I feel.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「征北表如此。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The General Who Campaigns North's memorial is thus.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The memorial of the General Who Campaigns North is as follows.

sentences.zh: 省以慨然。

translations.literal: On reading it I am stirred with feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I have read it and am deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 誕及妻女，並可以庶人禮葬，並置守衛。」

translations.literal: Dan and his wife and daughters may all be buried with commoner rites, and guards shall be posted.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, his wife, and his daughters may be buried with commoners' rites, and guards shall be posted at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始四年，又更改葬，祭以少牢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi of Emperor Taizong, the burial was changed again and sacrifice was offered with the minor livestock rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, the tomb was restored and sacrifices were offered with the secondary livestock rite.

sentences.zh: 廬江王禕，字休秀，文帝第八子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang Yi, styled Xiuxiu, was the eighth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Lujiang, whose courtesy name was Xiuxiu, was the eighth son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，年十歲，封東海王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, at age ten, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, at age ten, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai with a fief of 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，以為侍中、後軍將軍，領石頭戍事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was made Palace Attendant, Rear General, and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he was made Palace Attendant and Rear General, and given command of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍將軍、南彭城、下邳二郡太守、散騎常侍，領戍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Champion General, Governor of the two commanderies of Nanpengcheng and Xiapi, and Regularly Attending Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, garrison command as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Champion General, governor of Nanpengcheng and Xiapi, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, retaining command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 出為會稽太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Kuaiji, general's rank as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as governor of Kuaiji, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷使持節、都督廣交二州荊州之始興臨安二郡諸軍事、車騎將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of all military affairs of the two provinces of Guang and Jiao and the two commanderies of Shixing and Lin'an in Jing Province, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pacifier of the Yue Central Commandant, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he was made Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Guang and Jiao provinces and Shixing and Lin'an commanderies in Jing Province, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Pacifier of the Yue, and governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 昔周室既盛，二叔流言，漢祚方隆，七蕃迷叛，斯實事彰往代，難興自古。

translations.literal: In old times when the Zhou house was flourishing, the two uncles spread slander; when Han's fortune was rising, the seven feudal domains strayed into rebellion—such things are manifest in past ages; such difficulties have arisen since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou flourished, the Duke of Zhou was slandered by the two uncles; when the Han rose, the seven princely domains rebelled—history shows such crises are as old as empire itself.

sentences.zh: 雖聖賢御極，宇內紓患。

translations.literal: Though sages and worthies ascended the throne, within the realm they eased calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Even sage rulers, once enthroned, must still pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 太尉廬江王藉慶皇枝，蚤升寵樹，幼無立德，長缺修聲，淡薄親情，厚結行路，狎昵群細，疏澀人士。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Prince of Lujiang, relying on the felicitous imperial branch, rose early to favor's tree; in youth he established no virtue, in maturity he lacked cultivated reputation; he was cold toward kin, thick in bond with passing strangers; intimate with riffraff, estranged and blunt toward gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commander, Prince of Lujiang, rose early on his birth as an imperial prince; as a youth he built no virtue, as a man he won no good name. He was cold to kin yet warm to strangers, intimate with petty men and distant from worthy gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 自朕撥亂定宇，受命應天，實尚敦睦，克敷友于，故崇殊爵，超居上臺。

translations.literal: Since I settled disorder and fixed the realm, received the mandate and answered Heaven, I truly honored kindness and kinship and was able to spread brotherly love; therefore I raised extraordinary rank and set him above the upper terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When I pacified the realm and received Heaven's mandate, I prized kinship and brotherly harmony and therefore elevated him to the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 而公常懷不平，表於事蹟。

translations.literal: Yet you constantly harbored resentment, shown in deeds and traces.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have nursed grievance, and your conduct shows it.

sentences.zh: 公若德深望重，宜膺大統，朕初平暴亂，豈敢當璧，自然推符奉璽，天祚有歸。

translations.literal: If your virtue were deep and your weight of repute heavy, you ought to receive the great succession; when I first pacified violent disorder, how would I dare to hold the jade disk—naturally one would pass the tally and present the seal, and Heaven's fortune would have its due place.
translations.idiomatic: If your virtue and standing truly outweighed mine, the throne should have been yours; when I first seized power amid chaos I hardly dared claim the Mandate—you would have received the seal by acclamation and Heaven's favor would have found its rightful lord.

sentences.zh: 且朕雖居尊極，不敢自恃，宗室之事，無不諮公。

translations.literal: Moreover, though I occupy the summit of honor, I dare not rely on myself—in matters of the imperial clan there was nothing in which I did not consult you.
translations.idiomatic: Though I sit upon the throne, I have never presumed on my own judgment; on every matter touching the imperial clan I consulted you.

sentences.zh: 不虞志欲難滿，妄生窺怨，積慝在衿，遂謀社稷。

translations.literal: I did not anticipate that ambition is hard to satisfy; you rashly harbored covetous resentment, stored malice in your breast, and thus plotted against the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined your appetite could not be sated—you nursed secret grievance, clutched malice to your heart, and turned against the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 曩者四方遘禍，兵斥畿甸，搢紳憂惶，親賢同憤。

translations.literal: Formerly when calamity befell the four quarters and arms pressed the capital region, court officials were anxious and fearful, and kinsmen and worthies shared the same indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck from every quarter and armies massed at the capital, officials trembled and loyal kinsmen and ministers burned with righteous fury.

sentences.zh: 唯公獨幸厥災，深抃時難，晝則從禽遊肆，夜則縱酒弦歌，側耳視陰，企賊休問。

translations.literal: You alone rejoiced in that disaster and deeply clapped your hands at the hard times—by day you followed the hunt and roamed in pleasure; by night you let loose wine and strummed songs; you cocked your ear and watched the shadows, eagerly awaiting word that the rebels would prevail.
translations.idiomatic: You alone exulted in the catastrophe—hunting by day and feasting by night—straining to catch news from the shadows, praying the rebels would win.

sentences.zh: 司徒休仁等並各令弟，事兼家國，推鋒履險，各伐一方，蒙霜踐棘，辛勤已甚。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Xiuren and the rest, each your worthy younger brothers, their affairs embracing family and state, thrust forward spear-points and trod danger, each campaigning in one region, enduring frost and treading brambles—their toil was already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren, Steward of the Masses, and your other brothers each bore the burdens of throne and kin, took the spear-point into danger, and campaigned in separate realms through frost and thorn—their hardship was beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 況身被矢石，否泰難虞，悠悠之人，尚有信分。

translations.literal: How much more when one's body was struck by arrows and stones—fortune and misfortune hard to foresee—even unimportant people still had a sense of trust and duty.
translations.idiomatic: They faced arrows and stones with fortune and ruin hanging in the balance—yet even ordinary folk knew their obligation of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 公未曾有一函之使，遺半紙之書，志棄五弟，以餌仇賊。

translations.literal: You never once sent an envoy with one letter or a half sheet of writing—you resolved to abandon your five younger brothers to bait the enemy rebels.
translations.idiomatic: You never sent so much as a letter or half a page—you meant to sacrifice your five brothers as bait for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 自謂身非勳烈，義不參謀，必期凶逆道申，以圖輔相。

translations.literal: You considered yourself no meritorious hero and that duty did not require your counsel—you necessarily expected the way of the vicious rebels to prevail so you could seek the post of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming you were no battle hero and owed no counsel, you counted on the rebels' victory so you could become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 及皇威既震，群凶肅蕩，九有同慶，萬國含欣。

translations.literal: When imperial majesty had already shaken forth and the mass of villains was swept clean, the nine domains shared celebration and the myriad states held joy within.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial might prevailed and the rebels were crushed, the whole realm rejoiced and every land breathed relief.

sentences.zh: 而公容氣更沮，下帷晦跡，每覘天察宿，懷協左道，咒詛禱請，謹事邪巫，常被發跣足，稽首北極，遂圖畫朕躬，勒以名字，或加以矢刃，或烹之鼎鑊。

translations.literal: Yet your countenance grew more dejected; you lowered curtains and hid your tracks, constantly observing Heaven and inspecting the stars, harboring heterodox arts, cursing and praying, dutifully serving evil sorcerers, often with hair unbound and feet bare, kowtowing toward the North Star—you then painted my person, inscribed it with names, sometimes adding arrows and blades, sometimes boiling it in cauldrons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you only grew more sullen—you shut yourself away, scanned the heavens, embraced sorcery, and served wicked shamans, often with hair loose and feet bare, bowing to the Pole Star; you had my likeness painted, marked with names, pierced with blades, or boiled in pots.

sentences.zh: 公在江州，得一漢女，云知吉凶，能行厭咒，大設供養，朝夕拜伏，衣裝嚴整，敬事如神；

translations.literal: While you were in Jiangzhou you obtained a Han woman who claimed to know fortune and misfortune and could perform malign incantations; you made great offerings, bowing morning and evening, dress strict and orderly, serving her as a god;
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou you found a Han woman who claimed to read omens and cast malign spells; you lavished offerings on her, bowing day and night in formal dress and treating her like a deity;

sentences.zh: 令其祝詛孝武，并及崇憲，祈皇室危弱，統天稱己；

translations.literal: you had her pray curses against Emperor Xiaowu and also against Empress Dowager Chongxian, praying that the imperial house grow weak and perilous and that you alone hold Heaven and call yourself sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: you had her curse Emperor Xiaowu and Empress Dowager Chongxian alike, praying the dynasty would weaken so you might rule Heaven in your own name;

sentences.zh: 巫稱神旨，必得如願，後事發覺，委罪所生，徼幸｛危阝｝｛阝區｝，僅得自免。

translations.literal: The sorceress declared it divine will that your wish would surely be granted; later the matter was discovered, and you shifted blame onto your birth mother, narrowly escaping by a stroke of luck and barely saving yourself.
translations.idiomatic: The witch swore the gods would grant your wish; when the plot was exposed you blamed your birth mother and only narrowly escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 近又有道士張寶，為公見信，事既彰露，肆之於法。

translations.literal: Recently there was also the Daoist Zhang Bao, whom you trusted; once the matter was exposed, he was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: You also trusted a Daoist named Zhang Bao; when his plot was exposed, he was put to death by law.

sentences.zh: 公不知慚懼，猶加營理，遣左右二人，主掌殯含。

translations.literal: You knew neither shame nor fear, yet still extended your arrangements, sending two attendants to manage the burial provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Unashamed and unafraid, you went on making arrangements, dispatching two attendants to oversee funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 顯行邪志，罔顧吏司。

translations.literal: You openly pursued evil intent, heedless of the officials of law.
translations.idiomatic: You pursued your wicked designs openly, with no regard for the law.

sentences.zh: 又挾閹豎陳道明交關不逞，傳驛音意，投金散寶，以為信誓。

translations.literal: You also colluded with the eunuch Chen Daoming in illicit dealings, sending courier messages, casting gold and scattering jewels as pledge of faith.
translations.idiomatic: You also conspired with the eunuch Chen Daoming, exchanging messages by courier post and showering gold and jewels as pledges of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又使府史徐虎兒招引邊將，要結禁旅，規害台輔，圖犯宮掖。

translations.literal: You also had your clerk Xu Hu'er recruit border generals, win over the palace guard, plot harm against chief ministers, and plan to assault the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: You also sent your clerk Xu Hu'er to recruit border generals, win over the palace guard, target the chief ministers, and plot an assault on the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 公受性不仁，才非治用，昔忝江州，無稱被徵，前蒞會稽，以罪左黜。

translations.literal: By nature you are unkind; your talent is unfit for governance. Formerly you held Jiangzhou without distinction and were recalled; earlier you went to Kuaiji and were demoted to the left for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: You are unkind by nature and unfit to govern. You served at Jiangzhou without distinction and were recalled; later you were posted to Kuaiji and demoted for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 公稽古寡聞，嚴而無理，言不暢寒暑，惠不及帷房，朝野所輕，搢紳同侮，豈堪輔相之地，寧任蒞民之職，非唯一朝，有自來矣。

translations.literal: You are versed in antiquity yet narrow in hearing, stern yet without reason; your words do not flow through cold and heat, your kindness does not reach the inner chambers; court and countryside alike despise you, officials together hold you in contempt—you are hardly fit for the seat of chief minister, let alone the duty of governing the people; this is not of one reign alone—it has been so from the first.
translations.idiomatic: You affect learning yet know little, and are harsh without reason; your speech is graceless and your kindness never reaches home. Court and country alike despise you, and officials hold you in contempt—you are unfit to be chief minister, let alone govern the people; this has been true for years.

sentences.zh: 大明之世，迄於永光，公常留中，未嘗外撫，何以在今，方起嫌怨。

translations.literal: Throughout the Daming era down to Yongguang, you always remained at court and never went out to govern the regions—why now do you suddenly raise suspicion and resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the Daming era and into Yongguang you stayed at court and never held a provincial post—so why do you now nurse suspicion and grievance?

sentences.zh: 公少即長人，情無哀戚，侍拜長寧，從祀宗廟，顏無戚狀，淚不垂臉，兄弟長幼，靡有愛心。

translations.literal: From youth you have been grown in stature yet without sorrow in feeling; when attending obeisance at Changning and following sacrifice at the ancestral temple, your face showed no grieving aspect and tears did not fall upon your cheeks; among elder and younger brothers there was no loving heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though grown to manhood from youth, you have never known grief; at obeisance in Changning and rites at the ancestral temple your face showed no sorrow and no tear touched your cheek—you have no love for your brothers, elder or younger.

sentences.zh: 昔因孝武御筵置酒，心誠不著，於時義陽念遇本薄，遭公此譖，益被猜嫌。

translations.literal: Once at Emperor Xiaowu's imperial banquet with wine set out, your sincerity did not show; at that time Yiyang's regard and favor were already slight, and suffering this slander from you, he came under still greater suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Emperor Xiaowu's banquet your insincerity showed plainly; Yiyang was already lightly regarded at court, and after your slander he fell under still deeper suspicion.

sentences.zh: 朕當時狼狽，不暇自理，賴崇憲太后譬解百端，少蒙申亮，得免殃責。

translations.literal: I was then in distress and had no leisure to defend myself; relying on Empress Dowager Chongxian to explain in every way, I slightly received clearing and illumination and escaped blame and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I was then in such distress I could not defend myself; only Empress Dowager Chongxian's tireless explanations partly cleared my name and spared me punishment.

sentences.zh: 景和狂主，醜毒橫流，初誅宰輔，豺志方扇。

translations.literal: Jinghe the mad ruler—ugly poison flowed freely; he first executed chief ministers, and wolfish ambition was just rising.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jinghe the mad ruler, cruelty ran unchecked; he began by executing his chief ministers, and his wolfish ambition was just taking wing.

sentences.zh: 于建章宮召朕兄弟，逼酒使醉，公因酒勢，遂肆苦言，云朕及休仁，與太宰親數，往必清閒，贈貺豐厚。

translations.literal: At Jianzhang Palace he summoned us brothers and forced wine until we were drunk; you, riding the wine's force, then let loose bitter words, saying that I and Xiuren were on intimate terms with the Grand Counselor, that visits were always peaceful and leisurely, and gifts generous.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianzhang Palace he summoned us brothers and forced us to drink until drunk; emboldened by wine, you then accused me and Xiuren of intimacy with the Grand Counselor, claiming our visits were cozy and our gifts lavish.

sentences.zh: 朕當時惶駭，五內崩墜，於其語次，劣得小止。

translations.literal: I was then terrified and my five viscera collapsed; midway through his words I barely obtained a slight pause.
translations.idiomatic: I was terrified, my heart shattered within me, and only midway through his tirade did I gain a brief respite.

sentences.zh: 往又經在尋陽長公主第，兄弟共集，忽中坐忿怒，厲色見指，以朕行止出入，每不能同，若得稱心，規肆忿憾。

translations.literal: On another occasion we were gathered at the Xunyang Princess's residence, brothers together assembled; suddenly mid-seated you flared in anger, pointing with fierce countenance—because my comings and goings never matched yours, if you got your wish you would vent your wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Xunyang Princess's residence, with all of us brothers gathered, you suddenly erupted in mid-feast, pointing at me in fury—my every movement displeased you, and given the chance you would have unleashed your rage.

sentences.zh: 惟公此旨，蚤欲見滅，而天道愛善，朕獲南面，不長惡逆，挫公毒心。

translations.literal: By this intent of yours you long wished to see me destroyed; yet Heaven's way loves goodness—I obtained the south-facing throne, did not indulge evil rebels, and thwarted your poisonous heart.
translations.idiomatic: By your own admission you long wished me dead; yet Heaven favors the good—I took the throne, refused to indulge evil, and foiled your murderous designs.

sentences.zh: 自大明積費，國弊民凋，加景和奢虐，府藏罄盡。

translations.literal: Since the Daming era accumulated expenses, the state has weakened and the people withered; add Jinghe's luxury and cruelty, and the treasury stores were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Daming era the state has been drained by mounting costs and the people impoverished; Jinghe's extravagance and cruelty emptied the treasury altogether.

sentences.zh: 朕在位甫爾，恤義具瞻，仍值終阻蜂起，日耗萬金，公卿庶民，傾產歸獻。

translations.literal: I had just ascended the throne, compassion and righteousness looked to me, yet still met the Zhongshu rebellion rising like hornets, daily consuming ten thousand in gold; nobles and commoners emptied their estates to contribute.
translations.idiomatic: I had barely taken the throne when all eyes turned to me for mercy and justice, yet the Zhongshu rebellion erupted and gold poured out by the ten thousand daily—nobles and commoners alike stripped their estates to give.

sentences.zh: 積受台奉，貲畜優廣。

translations.literal: You accumulated received terrace salaries; wealth and livestock were abundant and broad.
translations.idiomatic: You amassed your court stipends until your wealth and livestock overflowed.

sentences.zh: 朕踐阼之初，公請故太宰東傳余錢，見入數百萬，內不充養，外不助國，散賜諂諛，遍惠趨隸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of my accession you requested the late Grand Counselor's east-transmitted remaining money—visible income in the millions—yet inwardly you did not support your household, outwardly you did not aid the state; you scattered gifts to flatterers and broadly favored runners and slaves.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of my reign you claimed the late Grand Counselor's remaining funds in the east—millions in plain sight—yet spent nothing on your household or the state, showering sycophants and lackeys instead.

sentences.zh: 推心考行，事類斯比。

translations.literal: Examining your conduct with an open heart, matters are of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Judge your conduct honestly, and this is the pattern throughout.

sentences.zh: 群小交構，遂生異圖，籍籍之義，轉盈民口。

translations.literal: Petty men intertwined plots, and different schemes arose; buzzing talk overflowed the mouths of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Petty schemers wove plots and treasonous designs spread until rumor filled every mouth in the land.

sentences.zh: 公若地居衡寄，任專八柄，德育於民，勳高於物，勢不自安，於事為可。

translations.literal: If you held a pivotal position, wielded the eight powers exclusively, nourished the people with virtue, and your merit towered above things—unease would not be self-generated; in the matter it would be understandable.
translations.idiomatic: Had you held real power, commanded the eight imperial prerogatives, governed with virtue, and towered in merit above all others, restlessness might be understandable.

sentences.zh: 公既才均櫟木，牽以曲全，因高無民，得守虛靜，而坐作凶咎，自囗深釁。

translations.literal: Your talent is equal to corkwood; you were pulled along to survive by bending; high yet without the people, you could keep empty quiet—yet you sat creating evil omens and brought deep offense upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your talent is useless as corkwood; you were kept on only by bending; elevated yet without popular support, you could have lived in quiet—but instead you courted evil and brought deep guilt upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 由朕誠感無素，爰至於此，永尋多難，惋慨實深。

translations.literal: Because my sincerity and feeling lacked constancy, it has come to this; forever tracing many hardships, regret and sighing are truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Because I lacked constancy in my goodwill, it has come to this—and looking back on so many trials, my grief and regret run very deep.

sentences.zh: 凡人所行，各有本志。

translations.literal: All men's conduct has its root intent.
translations.idiomatic: Every man's actions spring from his own intent.

sentences.zh: 朕博愛尚仁，為日已久，尚能含讎恕辠，著於觸事，豈容於公，不相隱忍。

translations.literal: I broadly love and esteem benevolence—the days have been long; I can still contain enmity and forgive crimes, shown in whatever I touch—how could I toward you fail to forbear?
translations.idiomatic: I have long cherished broad love and benevolence, and have forgiven enemies time and again in every matter I touch—how could I not have forborne with you?

sentences.zh: 但禍萌易漸，去惡宜疾，負荷之重，寧得坐觀。

translations.literal: But calamity's sprout spreads easily; removing evil should be swift—the burden's weight—how can one sit and watch?
translations.idiomatic: But evil spreads quickly once it takes root, and must be cut down at once; bearing the weight of the realm, how can I sit idle?

sentences.zh: 且蔓草難除，燎火須撲，狡扇之徒，宜時誅剪。

translations.literal: Moreover, creeping weeds are hard to remove and spreading fire must be beaten out; cunning agitators should be timely cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Weeds are hard to uproot and fire must be stamped out at once—cunning instigators must be cut down without delay.

sentences.zh: 已詔司戮，肅正典刑。

translations.literal: I have already ordered the Minister of Justice to solemnly rectify the penal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered the Minister of Justice to enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 公身居戚長，情禮兼至，准之常科，顧有惻怛，宜少申國憲，以弔不臧。

translations.literal: You as a kin elder—feeling and ritual both utmost; measured against usual statutes there is compassion; you should slightly receive the state's law to mourn the ungood.
translations.idiomatic: As an elder kinsman you deserve both affection and ceremony; by ordinary law there would be compassion—but some measure of punishment is owed for your wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 今以淮南、宣城、歷陽三郡還立南豫州，降公為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史，削邑千戶，侍中、王如故。

translations.literal: Now from the three commanderies of Huainan, Xuancheng, and Liyang I restore Southern Yu Province; I demote you to General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commissioner with the Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Southern Yu Province; I reduce your fief by one thousand households; Palace Attendant and prince's rank remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: I now reestablish Southern Yu Province from Huainan, Xuancheng, and Liyang commanderies, demote you to General of Chariots and Cavalry with commissioner rank equal to the Three Excellencies and governor of Southern Yu, cut your fief by 1,000 households, and leave your titles as Palace Attendant and prince unchanged.

sentences.zh: 出鎮宣城，上遣腹心楊運長領兵防衛。

translations.literal: He went out to garrison Xuancheng; the emperor sent his trusted man Yang Yunchang to lead troops in guard and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Xuancheng, he was placed under guard by the emperor's trusted agent Yang Yunchang and an armed escort.

sentences.zh: 同黨柳欣慰、徐虎兒、陳道明、寗敬之、閭丘邈之、樊平祖、孟敬祖並伏誅。

translations.literal: Co-conspirators Liu Xinwei, Xu Hu'er, Chen Daoming, Ning Jingzhi, Luqiu Miaozhi, Fan Pingzu, and Meng Jingzu were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His co-conspirators Liu Xinwei, Xu Hu'er, Chen Daoming, Ning Jingzhi, Luqiu Miaozhi, Fan Pingzu, and Meng Jingzu were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，上又令有司奏：「禕忿懟有怨言，請免官，削爵土，付宛陵縣獄，依法窮治。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year the emperor again had the relevant offices memorialize: "Yi harbors resentment and angry words; we request removal from office, stripping of rank and fief, delivery to Wannling county prison, and exhaustive punishment according to law."
translations.idiomatic: The following sixth month the emperor ordered a memorial: "Prince Yi nurses resentment and speaks rebelliously; we request his dismissal, stripping of rank and fief, imprisonment in Wannling county, and full prosecution under law."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乃遣大鴻臚持節，兼宗正為副奉詔責禕，逼令自殺，時年三十五，即葬宣城。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent the Grand Herald bearing the staff, with the Director of the Imperial Clan as deputy, to deliver the edict rebuking Yi and force him to commit suicide; he was thirty-five years old and was buried at once in Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent the Grand Herald with imperial staff and the Director of the Imperial Clan as deputy to deliver an edict condemning Prince Yi and order his suicide. He was thirty-five and was buried at Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 子充明，輔國將軍、南彭城、東莞二郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Chongming was General Who Supports the State and Governor of the two commanderies of Nanpengcheng and Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongming served as General Who Supports the State and governor of Nanpengcheng and Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 廢徙新安歙縣。

translations.literal: Deposed, he was exiled to She county in Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: After the deposition he was exiled to She county in Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，聽還京邑。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended the throne, he was permitted to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he was allowed to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明二年卒，時年二十八，無子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming under Emperor Shun he died, at age twenty-eight, without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shengming year 2 of Emperor Shun, at age twenty-eight, leaving no sons.

sentences.zh: 武昌王渾，字休淵，文帝第十子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Wuchang Hun, styled Xiuyuan, was the tenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hun of Wuchang, whose courtesy name was Xiuyuan, was the tenth son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年，年九歲，封汝陰王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, at age nine, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ruyin with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, at age nine, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ruyin with a fief of 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 為後軍將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was made Rear General and given the additional title of Regularly Attending Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Rear General with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 索虜南寇，破汝陰郡，徙渾為武昌王。

translations.literal: The northern barbarians invaded south, broke Ruyin commandery, and Hun was transferred to Prince of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians invaded and overran Ruyin commandery, Hun was transferred to the title Prince of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 少而凶戾，嘗出石頭，怨左右人，援防身刀斫之。

translations.literal: From youth he was fierce and cruel; once leaving Shitou he grew angry at his attendants, drew his personal guard sword, and hacked at them.
translations.idiomatic: Violent and cruel from boyhood, he once left Shitou in a rage and hacked at his attendants with his personal sword.

sentences.zh: 元兇弑立，以為中書令。

translations.literal: When the prime villain murdered and enthroned himself, Hun was made Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper Liu Shao seized the throne, Hun was made Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 山陵夕，裸身露頭，往散騎省戲，因彎弓射通直郎周朗，中其枕，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: On the eve of the imperial tomb rites he went naked with head bare to the Scattered Cavalry section to play, then bent his bow and shot Direct Attendant Zhou Lang, hitting his pillow, and took it as laughter and sport.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the burial rites he went naked and bareheaded to the Scattered Cavalry offices for sport, bent his bow, and shot Direct Attendant Zhou Lang in the pillow—and laughed.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，授征虜將軍、南彭城、東海二郡太守，出鎮京口。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, Hun was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Governor of the two commanderies of Nanpengcheng and Donghai, and went out to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Hun was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians, governor of Nanpengcheng and Donghai, and posted to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 上遣員外散騎侍郎戴明寶詰渾曰：「我與汝親則同氣，義則君臣，遣任西蕃，以同磐石，云何一旦反欲見圖？

translations.literal: The emperor sent Extraordinary Cadet Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry Dai Mingbao to question Hun, saying: "Between us in kinship we share the same breath; in righteousness we are monarch and minister. I sent you to the western frontier as firm as bedrock—how could you suddenly turn and plot against me?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Dai Mingbao, Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, to rebuke Prince Hun: "We are brothers by blood and sovereign and subject by duty. I posted you to the western frontier as my bedrock—how could you turn against me?

sentences.zh: 文檄處分，事蹟炳然，不忠不義，乃可至此。

translations.literal: The written proclamations and dispositions—the deeds and traces are bright and clear; disloyal and unrighteous—you have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Your proclamations and actions speak for themselves—disloyalty and treachery could go no further.

sentences.zh: 豈唯天道助順，逆志難充，如其凶圖獲逞，天下誰當相容？

translations.literal: Is it not only that Heaven's way aids the obedient and rebellious intent is hard to fulfill? If your evil plot were to succeed, who under Heaven would tolerate you?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven aids the loyal and thwarts rebellion—if your treason succeeded, who under Heaven would accept you?

sentences.zh: 前事不遠，足為鑒戒。

translations.literal: Recent events are not far off—sufficient as mirror and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Recent history is near enough to serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 加以頻歲釁難，非起外人，唯應相與厲精，以固七百。

translations.literal: Moreover, in successive years strife and hardship have arisen—not from outsiders; we should only together refine our spirit to solidify the seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, rebellion after rebellion has come from within our own house; we should together steel ourselves to preserve the dynasty's seven-century legacy.

sentences.zh: 汝忽復構此，良可悲惋。

translations.literal: You suddenly construct this again—truly lamentable and regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: That you would plot this again is truly lamentable.

sentences.zh: 國雖有典，我亦何忍極法，好自將養，以保松、喬之壽。」

translations.literal: Though the state has its statutes, how could I bear to apply the extreme law? Take good care of yourself and preserve the longevity of Song and Qiao."
translations.idiomatic: Though the law is strict, I cannot bring myself to punish you to the full—take care of yourself and live out your natural span."

sentences.zh: 逼令自殺，即葬襄陽，時年十七。

translations.literal: He was forced to commit suicide and was buried at once in Xiangyang; he was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take his own life and was buried at Xiangyang. He was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，聽還葬母江太妃墓次。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming he was permitted to be reburied beside the tomb of his mother, Lady Jiang the Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming he was permitted reburial beside the tomb of his mother, Lady Jiang the Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追封為武昌縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Hun was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuchang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuchang county.

sentences.zh: 王翼之，字季弼，琅邪臨沂人，晉黃門侍郎徽之孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Yizhi, styled Jibi, was a man of Linyi in Langya and grandson of Jin's Yellow Gate Attendant Huizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yizhi, whose courtesy name was Jibi, was from Linyi in Langya and grandson of Huizhi, Yellow Gate Attendant under Jin.

sentences.zh: 官至御史中丞，會稽太守，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Censor-in-Chief, Governor of Kuaiji, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Censor-in-Chief, governor of Kuaiji, and governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Su (Solemn) zi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous epithet was Su (Solemn).

sentences.zh: 海陵王休茂，文帝第十四子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Hailing Xiumao was the fourteenth son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao of Hailing was the fourteenth son of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 孝建二年，年十一，封海陵王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaojian, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year 2, at age eleven, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing with a fief of 2,000 households.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，以為使持節、都督雍、梁、南北秦四州、郢州之竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、北中郎將、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of all military affairs of the four provinces of Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin and the two commanderies of Jingling and Sui in Ying Province, Northern Central Commandant, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he was made Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin provinces and Jingling and Sui commanderies in Ying Province, Northern Central Commandant, Pacifier of the Barbarians, and governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 進號左將軍，增邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced in title to Left General and his fief was increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left General and his fief increased by 1,000 households.

sentences.zh: 時司馬庾深之行府事，休茂性急疾，欲自專，深之及主帥每禁之，常懷忿怒。

translations.literal: At that time Staff Major Yu Shenzhi ran the prefecture's affairs; Xiumao was impatient by nature and wished to act alone; Shenzhi and the chief administrator often restrained him, and he constantly nursed anger.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Major Yu Shenzhi then ran the administration; impulsive by nature, Prince Xiumao wanted sole control, but Shenzhi and the chief administrator constantly checked him, and he nursed a growing rage.

sentences.zh: 左右張伯超至所親愛，多罪過，主帥常加呵責，伯超懼罪，謂休茂曰：「主帥密疏官罪過，欲以啟聞，如此，恐無好。」

translations.literal: His attendant Zhang Bochao was most beloved; he had many faults and the chief administrator often scolded him. Bochao feared punishment and said to Xiumao: "The chief administrator secretly reports Your Highness's faults and wishes to inform the court—like this, I fear no good outcome."
translations.idiomatic: His favorite attendant Zhang Bochao had many faults and was often scolded by the chief administrator. Fearing punishment, Bochao told Prince Xiumao: "The chief administrator is secretly reporting your misconduct to the court—at this rate, nothing good awaits us."

sentences.zh: 休茂曰：「為何計？」

translations.literal: Xiumao said: "What plan is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao asked: "What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 伯超曰：「唯當殺行事及主帥，且舉兵自衛。

translations.literal: Bochao said: "We must only kill the acting administrator and the chief administrator, and moreover raise troops in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Bochao said: "We must kill the acting administrator and the chief administrator, then raise troops in our own defense.

sentences.zh: 此去都數千里，縱大事不成，不失入虜中為王。」

translations.literal: This place is several thousand li from the capital; even if the great affair does not succeed, we will not lose the option of entering barbarian lands to be kings."
translations.idiomatic: We are thousands of li from the capital—even if the revolt fails, we can still flee north and become kings among the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 休茂從之。

translations.literal: Xiumao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao agreed.

sentences.zh: 夜挾伯超及左右黃靈期、蔡捷世、滕穆之、王寶龍、來承道、彭叔兒、魏公子、陳伯兒、張駟奴、楊興、劉保、餘雙等，率夾轂隊，於城內殺典籤楊慶，出金城，殺司馬庾深之、典籤戴雙。

translations.literal: By night he took Bochao and his attendants Huang Lingqi, Cai Jieshi, Teng Muzhi, Wang Baolong, Lai Chengdao, Peng Shu'er, Wei Gongzi, Chen Bo'er, Zhang Sinu, Yang Xing, Liu Bao, Yu Shuang, and the rest, led the Jiaogu unit, killed Registrar Yang Qing inside the city, exited through Jincheng gate, and killed Staff Major Yu Shenzhi and Registrar Dai Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: That night he took Bochao and his followers Huang Lingqi, Cai Jieshi, Teng Muzhi, Wang Baolong, Lai Chengdao, Peng Shu'er, Wei Gongzi, Chen Bo'er, Zhang Sinu, Yang Xing, Liu Bao, Yu Shuang, and others, led the Jiaogu guard, killed Registrar Yang Qing inside the city, exited through Jincheng gate, and killed Staff Major Yu Shenzhi and Registrar Dai Shuang.

sentences.zh: 集徵兵眾，建牙馳檄，使佐吏上車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加黃鉞。

translations.literal: He gathered levied troops, raised the command banner and sent flying proclamations, and had his aide submit a petition for Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commissioner with the Ceremony Equal to the Three Excellencies, with the Yellow Battle-Axe added.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered troops, raised his banner and issued proclamations, and had an aide petition for the titles Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner Equal to the Three Excellencies with the Yellow Battle-Axe.

sentences.zh: 侍讀博士荀銑諫爭，見殺。

translations.literal: Lecturer Doctor Xun Xian remonstrated and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturer Doctor Xun Xian remonstrated with him and was killed.

sentences.zh: 伯超專任軍政，殺害自己。

translations.literal: Bochao monopolized military and civil affairs and killed at his own discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Bochao seized control of military and civil affairs and slaughtered whomever he chose.

sentences.zh: 休茂左右曹萬期挺身斫休茂，被創走，見殺。

translations.literal: Xiumao's attendant Cao Wanqi rushed forward and hacked at Xiumao; wounded, he fled and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao's attendant Cao Wanqi lunged forward and struck at him; wounded, Cao fled and was killed.

sentences.zh: 休茂出城行營，諮議參軍沈暢之等率眾閉門拒之。

translations.literal: Xiumao went out of the city to inspect the camp; Consultant Staff Officer Shen Changzhi and the rest led troops, shut the gates, and resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiumao went out to inspect his camp, Consultant Shen Changzhi and others led troops to shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 休茂馳還，不得入。

translations.literal: Xiumao galloped back but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao galloped back but could not re-enter the city.

sentences.zh: 義成太守薛繼考為休茂盡力攻城，殺傷甚眾，暢之不能自固，遂得入城，斬暢之及同謀數十人。

translations.literal: Yicheng Governor Xue Jikao exerted all effort for Xiumao in assaulting the city; casualties were very many; Changzhi could not hold firm, and Jikao thus entered the city and beheaded Changzhi and several dozen co-conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng governor Xue Jikao fought hard for Prince Xiumao and stormed the city with heavy casualties; Shen Changzhi could not hold out, and Xue broke in and beheaded Changzhi and dozens of conspirators.

sentences.zh: 其日，參軍尹玄慶起義，攻休茂，生禽之，將出中門斬首，時年十七。

translations.literal: That same day Staff Officer Yin Xuanqing raised a loyal force, attacked Xiumao, captured him alive, and was about to exit the central gate to behead him; he was seventeen years old.
translations.idiomatic: That same day staff officer Yin Xuanqing raised a loyal force, attacked Prince Xiumao, captured him alive, and was about to behead him at the central gate. He was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 母妻皆自殺，同黨悉伏誅。

translations.literal: His mother and wife all committed suicide; co-conspirators were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother and wife killed themselves, and all his co-conspirators were put to death.

sentences.zh: 城中撓亂，無相統領。

translations.literal: The city was in turmoil with no one to lead overall.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell into chaos with no one in command.

sentences.zh: 時尚書右僕射劉秀之弟恭之為休茂中兵參軍，眾共推行府州事。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Liu Xiuzhi's younger brother Gongzhi was Xiumao's Middle Army Staff Officer; the crowd jointly pushed him to administer prefecture and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gongzhi, younger brother of Minister of Works Liu Xiuzhi and Prince Xiumao's middle army staff officer, was pressed by the crowd to take charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 繼考以兵肋恭之，使作啟事云立義，自乘驛還都，上以為永嘉王子仁北中郎諮議參軍、河南太守，封冠軍縣侯，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: Jikao coerced Gongzhi with troops, made him compose a memorial claiming loyalty to the righteous cause, and himself rode the courier post back to the capital; the emperor made him Consultant Staff Officer to the Northern Central Commandant for Prince Ren of Yongjia, Governor of Henan, enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun county with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jikao forced Gongzhi at sword-point to write a memorial claiming loyalty, then rode post-haste to the capital; the emperor rewarded him with the posts of consultant to Prince Ren of Yongjia's Northern Central Commandant and governor of Henan, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Guanjun with a fief of 400 households.

sentences.zh: 尋事泄，伏誅。

translations.literal: Soon the matter leaked out and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the plot was exposed and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 恭之坐繫尚方。

translations.literal: Gongzhi was imprisoned for his offense at the Shangfang.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi was imprisoned in the Shangfang workshop for his role in the affair.

sentences.zh: 以玄慶為射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Yin Xuanqing was made Commandant of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xuanqing was appointed Commandant of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.

sentences.zh: 有司奏絕休茂屬籍，貶姓為留，上不許。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized to expunge Xiumao from the clan register and degrade his surname to Liu; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials petitioned to strike Prince Xiumao from the imperial clan register and reduce his surname to Liu, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 即葬襄陽。

translations.literal: He was immediately buried at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at once at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 庾深之，字彥靜，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Shenzhi, styled Yanjing, was a man of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shenzhi, whose courtesy name was Yanjing, was from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 以事先朝見知。

translations.literal: Through service to the former court he gained recognition.
translations.idiomatic: He won notice through service to the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，自輔國長史為長沙內史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia he went from Senior Aide to the General Who Supports the State to Administrator of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia he was promoted from senior aide to the General Who Supports the State to administrator of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 南郡王義宣為荊、湘二州，加深之寧朔將軍，督湘州七郡。

translations.literal: When Prince Yixuan of Nanjun held Jing and Xiang provinces, Shenzhi was further made General Who Pacifies the North and overseer of the seven commanderies of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yixuan of Nanjun governed Jing and Xiang, Shenzhi was further made General Who Pacifies the North and put in charge of Xiangzhou's seven commanderies.

sentences.zh: 明年，義宣為逆，深之據巴陵拒之。

translations.literal: The following year Yixuan rebelled; Shenzhi held Baling and resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Prince Yixuan rebelled; Shenzhi held Baling and resisted him.

sentences.zh: 轉休茂司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Xiumao's Staff Major.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as staff major to Prince Xiumao.

sentences.zh: 見害之旦，子孫亦死。

translations.literal: On the morning he was killed, his descendants also died.
translations.idiomatic: On the morning he was killed, his children and grandchildren died as well.

sentences.zh: 追贈深之冠軍將軍、雍州刺史，荀銑員外散騎侍郎，曹萬期始平太守。

translations.literal: Shenzhi was posthumously awarded General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Governor of Yong; Xun Xian was made Extraordinary Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, and Cao Wanqi Governor of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi was posthumously made General Who Overcomes the Enemy and governor of Yong; Xun Xian was made extraordinary gentleman of the scattered cavalry, and Cao Wanqi governor of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，以為使持節、都督南徐、徐、南兗、兗四州諸軍事、鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the turmoil, Xiufan was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over the military affairs of Southern Xu, Xu, Southern Yan, and Yan provinces, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Southern Xu, with one set of pipes and drums granted.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming restored order, Prince Xiufan was made bearer of the staff, commander over Southern Xu, Xu, Southern Yan, and Yan, General Who Pacifies the North, and governor of Southern Xu, with a full ceremonial guard of pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 時薛安都據彭城反叛，遣從子索兒南侵，休範進據廣陵，督北討諸軍事，加南兗州刺史，進征北大將軍，加散騎常侍，還京口，解兗州，增邑二千戶，受五百戶。

translations.literal: At that time Xue Anadu held Pengcheng in rebellion and sent his nephew Suo'er south to invade; Xiufan advanced and seized Guangling, supervised the northern punitive armies, was further made Governor of Southern Yan, promoted to Grand General Who Campaigns North, given the additional title Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, returned to Jingkou, relinquished Yanzhou, had his fief increased by two thousand households, and received five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Anadu held Pengcheng in revolt and sent his nephew Suo'er south to raid, Prince Xiufan advanced to Guangling, took command of the northern punitive armies, was further made governor of Southern Yan and promoted to Grand General Who Campaigns North with the additional title regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; he returned to Jingkou, gave up Yanzhou, and received a fief increase of 2,000 households plus 500 more.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，征為中書監、中軍將軍、揚州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi he was summoned to be Director of the Secretariat, Central Army General, and Governor of Yangzhou, retaining his regular attendant title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi he was recalled as director of the secretariat, central army general, and governor of Yangzhou, keeping his regular attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為使持節、都督江、郢、司、廣、交五州、豫州之西陽、新蔡、晉熙、湘州之始興四郡諸軍事、征南大將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: The following year he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander over the military affairs of Jiang, Ying, Si, Guang, and Jiao provinces and the four commanderies of Xiyang and Xincai in Yuzhou, Jinxi, and Shixing in Xiangzhou, Grand General Who Campaigns South, and Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out as bearer of the staff, commander over Jiang, Ying, Si, Guang, and Jiao and the four commanderies of Xiyang, Xincai, Jinxi, and Shixing, Grand General Who Campaigns South, and governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司，未拜，改授都督南徐、徐、南兗、兗、青、冀六州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、南徐州刺史，持節、常侍、開府如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was further given an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies; before accepting it he was reassigned as Commander over the military affairs of Southern Xu, Xu, Southern Yan, Yan, Qing, and Ji provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Governor of Southern Xu, retaining bearer of the staff, regular attendant, and open establishment as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon granted an establishment equal to the Three Excellencies, but before taking it was reassigned to command Southern Xu, Xu, Southern Yan, Yan, Qing, and Ji as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and governor of Southern Xu, keeping bearer of the staff, regular attendant, and open establishment unchanged.

sentences.zh: 未拜，以驃騎大將軍還為江州，進督越州諸軍事，給三望車一乘。

translations.literal: Before accepting the appointment he returned to Jiangzhou as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, was further made overseer of the military affairs of Yuezhou, and granted one Sanwang carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the new post he returned to Jiangzhou as Grand General of Agile Cavalry, was further put in charge of Yuezhou's military affairs, and given one Sanwang carriage.

sentences.zh: 太宗遺詔，進位司空，改常侍為侍中，加班劍三十人。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ming's deathbed edict he was promoted to Minister of Works, his regular attendant title was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and thirty sword-bearing guards were added.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's deathbed edict promoted him to Minister of Works, changed his regular attendant title to attendant-in-ordinary, and added thirty sword-bearing guards.

sentences.zh: 休範素凡訥，少知解，不為諸兄所齒遇。

translations.literal: Xiufan was by nature crude and slow of speech, with little understanding, and was not treated as an equal by his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiufan was dull and inarticulate by nature, slow-witted, and none of his elder brothers treated him as an equal.

sentences.zh: 太宗常指左右人謂王景文曰：「休範人才不及此，以我弟故，生便富貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming often pointed at the attendants around him and said to Wang Jingwen: "Xiufan's talent does not match these men; because he is my younger brother, he was born to wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming often gestured at the men around him and told Wang Jingwen: "Prince Xiufan's talent does not match these men; because he is my younger brother, he was born to wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 釋氏願生王家，良有以也。」

translations.literal: The Buddha's wish to be reborn in a royal house—there is good reason for it."
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha's wish to be reborn in a royal house—there is good reason for that."

sentences.zh: 及太宗晚年，晉平王休祐以狠戾致禍，建安王休仁以權逼不見容，巴陵王休若素得人情，又以此見害。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's later years Prince Xiuyou of Jinping brought disaster through savage cruelty; Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was not tolerated because his power pressed too hard; Prince Xiuruo of Baling had always won men's hearts, yet for that very reason was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's later years Prince Xiuyou of Jinping brought ruin through savage cruelty; Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was destroyed because his power was too threatening; Prince Xiuruo of Baling had always won men's hearts, yet for that very reason was killed.

sentences.zh: 唯休範謹澀無才能，不為物情所向，故得自保；

translations.literal: Only Xiufan, cautious and awkward and without ability, was not favored by public sentiment, and so was able to preserve himself;
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Xiufan, cautious, awkward, and without talent, drew no following among men, and so survived;

sentences.zh: 而常懷憂懼，恆慮禍及。

translations.literal: yet he constantly harbored worry and fear, always dreading that disaster would reach him.
translations.idiomatic: yet he lived in constant dread, always fearing that disaster would reach him.

sentences.zh: 及太宗晏駕，主幼時艱，素族當權，近習秉政，休範自謂宗戚莫二，應居宰輔，事既不至，怨憤彌結。
