translations.literal: When Emperor Ming passed away, the ruler was young and the times hard; humble clans held power and close favorites governed. Xiufan considered himself without peer among the imperial kin and fit to stand among the chief ministers; when this did not come to pass, resentment and anger grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, the throne passed to a child in troubled times; low-born families held power and court favorites ruled. Prince Xiufan believed himself without peer among the imperial kin and entitled to a seat among the chief ministers; when that failed to happen, his resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 招引勇士，繕治器械，行人經過尋陽者，莫不降意折節，重加問遺，囗囗留則傾身接引，厚相資給。

translations.literal: He recruited brave warriors and repaired weapons. Travelers passing through Xunyang all lowered their pride and bent their manner; he questioned them closely and sent them rich gifts; if they stayed he received them with full devotion and supplied them generously.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited warriors and repaired weapons. Every traveler passing through Xunyang was met with lowered pride and courtesy, rich gifts and repeated inquiries; those who stayed were received with full devotion and supplied generously.

sentences.zh: 於是遠近同應，從者如歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon men near and far responded alike, and followers came as though returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Men near and far answered his call, and followers gathered as though returning home.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其有異志，密相防禦，雖未表形跡，而釁難已成。

translations.literal: The court knew he harbored a different intent and secretly guarded against him; though his actions had not yet shown openly, the breach and disaster were already formed.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew he harbored rebellious intent and secretly guarded against him; though he had not yet acted openly, the breach was already made.

sentences.zh: 母荀太妃薨，葬廬山，以示不還之志。

translations.literal: When his mother, Consort Dowager Xun, died, he buried her on Mount Lu to show his resolve not to return.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother, Consort Dowager Xun, died, he buried her on Mount Lu to signal his resolve never to return.

sentences.zh: 解侍中。

translations.literal: He was relieved of the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from the post of attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 夫治政任賢，宜親疏相輔，得其經緯，則結繩可及；

translations.literal: Now, in governing the state and employing the worthy, close and distant should assist one another; if one grasps the warp and woof of affairs, even knotting cords to govern would suffice;
translations.idiomatic: In governing the state and employing the worthy, kin near and far should assist one another; grasp the warp and woof of affairs, and even rule by knotted cords would suffice;

sentences.zh: 失其規矩，則危亡可期。

translations.literal: lose the measure and rule, and peril and ruin may be expected.
translations.idiomatic: lose measure and rule, and ruin is near at hand.

sentences.zh: 漢承戰國之餘，傷周室衰殄，立磐石之宗，而致七國之亂。

translations.literal: Han inherited the aftermath of the Warring States, grieved at the Zhou house's decline and extinction, established princes firm as bedrock, and thereby brought on the Rebellion of the Seven States.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited the wreckage of the Warring States, mourned the Zhou house's decline, enfeoffed princes firm as bedrock, and thereby brought on the Rebellion of the Seven States.

sentences.zh: 魏革漢典，創於前失，遂使諸王絕朝聘之禮，是以根疏葉枯，政移異族。

translations.literal: Wei reformed Han institutions, taking its start from earlier failures, and thus made the princes cut off the rites of court audience and tribute; hence the roots grew sparse and the leaves withered, and government passed to another race.
translations.idiomatic: Wei reformed Han institutions to correct earlier failures, yet cut the princes off from court audience and tribute; the roots thinned, the leaves withered, and power passed to another people.

sentences.zh: 今宗室衰微，自昔未有，泰寧之世，足以為譬。

translations.literal: Today the imperial house is enfeebled as never before in memory; the age of Taining is warning enough.
translations.idiomatic: Today the imperial house is enfeebled as never before; the age of Taining is warning enough.

sentences.zh: 孤子忝枝皇族，預關興毀，雖欲忘言，其可得乎！

translations.literal: I, unworthy branch of the imperial clan, am involved in the rise and fall of the dynasty; though I wish to hold my tongue, how can I!
translations.idiomatic: I, unworthy branch of the imperial clan, am bound up in the dynasty's rise and fall; though I wish to hold my tongue, how can I!

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝升叡三光，滌紛四表。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, Emperor Wu, raised his brilliance to the three luminaries and washed away disorder on all four frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, the High Ancestor, raised his brilliance to the three luminaries and washed away disorder on every frontier.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝欽明冠古，資乾承曆，秉鉞西服，鳴鑾東京，搜賢選能，納奇賞異。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor, Emperor Wen, in reverent brilliance surpassed antiquity, received Heaven's mandate and inherited the calendar, grasped the battle-axe and pacified the west, sounded the imperial carriage in the eastern capital, sought out the worthy and selected the able, and welcomed the extraordinary and rewarded the unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor, in reverent brilliance surpassed antiquity, received Heaven's mandate, grasped the battle-axe and pacified the west, sounded the imperial carriage in the eastern capital, sought out the worthy, and welcomed and rewarded the extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 孝武皇帝歧嶷天縱，先機雷發，陵波靜亂，宏業中興，儲嗣不腆，遂貽禍難。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, precocious and Heaven-taught, seized the initiative like thunder, rode the waves and stilled disorder, and revived the great enterprise; yet the heir was unworthy, and so calamity was bequeathed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, precocious and Heaven-taught, seized the initiative like thunder, rode the waves and stilled disorder, and revived the great enterprise; yet the heir proved unworthy, and calamity followed.

sentences.zh: 于時建安王以家難頻遘，宜立長主，明皇帝恢郎淵懿，仁潤含遠，奉戴南面，允合天人。

translations.literal: At that time, because Prince Jian'an had repeatedly met with domestic calamity, it was fitting to establish an elder sovereign. Emperor Ming was broad-minded, deep and virtuous, benevolent and far-reaching in nurture; in receiving the southern throne he truly accorded with Heaven and men.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Jian'an had repeatedly met with domestic calamity, it was fitting to establish an elder sovereign. Emperor Ming was broad-minded, deep, and virtuous, benevolent and far-reaching; in taking the southern throne he truly accorded with Heaven and men.

sentences.zh: 而太尉以年長居卑，怨心形色，柳欣慰等規行不軌，事蹟披猖。

translations.literal: Yet the Grand Commandant, though senior in years, held a lower rank; resentment showed in his face and bearing. Liu Xinwei and others plotted unlawful conduct, and their deeds ran wild.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Grand Commandant, though the elder, held the lesser rank; resentment showed plainly on his face. Liu Xinwei and others plotted unlawful acts, and their deeds ran wild.

sentences.zh: 驃騎以忤顏失旨，應對不順，在蕃刻削，怨結人鬼。

translations.literal: The General of Agile Cavalry lost favor by offending the emperor's countenance and answering improperly; in his fief he was harshly cut back, and resentment bound men and ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: The General of Agile Cavalry lost favor by offending the emperor and answering improperly; in his fief he was harshly cut back, and resentment bound the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 先帝明於號令，豈枉法為親，二王之釁，實自由己。

translations.literal: The late emperor was clear in his commands—how would he bend the law for kin? The two princes' breach truly arose from themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was clear in his commands—would he bend the law for kin? The two princes' rebellion truly arose from themselves.

sentences.zh: 但司徒巴陵王勞謙為國，中流事難，有不世之勳，奉時如天，事兄猶父，非唯令友，信為國器。

translations.literal: But the Minister of Works, Prince Baling, toiled humbly for the state; in the crisis at the midstream he had unmatched merit, served the times as Heaven itself, treated his elder brother as a father, was not merely a fine companion, and truly was an instrument of the state.
translations.idiomatic: But Prince Baling, Minister of Works, toiled humbly for the state; in the crisis at the midstream he won unmatched merit, served the times as Heaven itself, treated his elder brother as a father, was not merely a fine companion but truly an instrument of the state.

sentences.zh: 唐叔之忠，而受管、蔡之罪，親戚哀憤，行路嗟歎。

translations.literal: Like Tang Shu's loyalty, yet he suffered the guilt of Guan and Cai; kinsmen mourned in anger, and travelers on the road sighed in lament.
translations.idiomatic: Like Tang Shu's loyalty, yet he suffered the guilt of Guan and Cai; kinsmen mourned in rage, and travelers on the road sighed in lament.

sentences.zh: 王地籍光潔，德厭民望，並無寸罪，受斃讒邪。

translations.literal: The prince's pedigree was bright and pure, his virtue satisfied the people's hopes; he had not a hair's breadth of guilt, yet was destroyed by slander and evil.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's lineage was bright and pure, his virtue satisfied the people's hopes; he had not a hair's breadth of guilt, yet was destroyed by slander and evil.

sentences.zh: 先帝穆於友于，留心親戚，去昔事平之後，面受詔誨，禮則君臣，樂則兄弟，升級賜賞，動不移年，撫慰孜孜，恆如不足，豈容一旦鬩牆，致此禍害，良有由也。

translations.literal: The late emperor was gracious in brotherly affection and attentive to his kin. After affairs were settled in the past, he received them face to face with edicts and instruction: in ceremony they were monarch and subject, in joy they were brothers; promotions and rewards came within the year, and his comforting care was tireless, always as though it were not enough. How could a sudden breach within the wall bring such calamity? There was truly a cause.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was gracious in brotherly affection and attentive to his kin. After affairs were settled, he received them face to face with edicts and instruction: in ceremony they were monarch and subject, in joy they were brothers; promotions and rewards came within the year, and his comforting care was tireless, always as though it were not enough. How could a sudden breach within the wall bring such calamity? There was truly a cause.

sentences.zh: 先帝寢疾彌年，體疲膳少，雖神照無虧，而慮有失德，補闕拾遺，責在左右。

translations.literal: The late emperor lay ill for years; his body was weary and his meals few. Though his divine clarity was undiminished, he feared lapses in virtue; to remedy omissions and gather what was lost was the duty of those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor lay ill for years; his body was weary and his meals few. Though his divine clarity was undiminished, he feared lapses in virtue; to remedy omissions and gather what was lost was the duty of those at his side.

sentences.zh: 于時出入臥內，唯有運長、道隆，群細無狀，因疾遘禍，見上不和，知無瘳拯，慮晏駕之日，長王作輔，奪其寵柄，不得自專。

translations.literal: At that time those who entered and left the inner bedchamber were only Yunzhang and Daolong—vile petty men without decency. Seizing on the illness to bring disaster, seeing the emperor's condition was not harmonious and knowing there was no recovery, they feared that on the day of his passing the elder prince would serve as regent, wrest away their favor and power, and leave them unable to act on their own.
translations.idiomatic: At that time only Yunzhang and Daolong entered and left the inner bedchamber—vile petty men without decency. Seizing on the illness to bring disaster, seeing the emperor's condition was grave and knowing there was no recovery, they feared that when he passed the elder prince would serve as regent, wrest away their favor and power, and leave them unable to act on their own.

sentences.zh: 是以內假帝旨，外托朝議，諛辭詭貌，萬類千端，升進姦回，屠斥賢哲，外矯天則，內誣人鬼。

translations.literal: Therefore within they borrowed the emperor's command, without they relied on court deliberation; with flattery and false faces, in myriad forms and a thousand guises, they promoted the wicked and perverse, slaughtered and expelled the worthy and wise, outwardly feigned Heaven's law, and inwardly slandered men and ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Within they borrowed the emperor's command; without they relied on court deliberation. With flattery and false faces, in myriad forms, they promoted the wicked, slaughtered and expelled the worthy, outwardly feigned Heaven's law, and inwardly slandered men and ghosts.

sentences.zh: 是以星紀違常，義望失度。

translations.literal: Hence the stars and seasons went against the norm, and righteousness and reputation lost their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the stars and seasons went against the norm, and righteousness and reputation lost their measure.

sentences.zh: 昔魏顆擇命，《春秋》美之；

translations.literal: Of old Wei Kuo chose his command—the Spring and Autumn Annals praise him;
translations.idiomatic: Of old Wei Kuo chose his command—the Spring and Autumn Annals praise him;

sentences.zh: 秦穆殉良，《詩》有明刺。

translations.literal: Duke Mu of Qin sacrificed the worthy—the Odes contain a clear rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu of Qin sacrificed the worthy—the Odes contain a clear rebuke.

sentences.zh: 臣子之節，得失必書，不及匡諫，猶以為罪。

translations.literal: The integrity of subject and minister requires that gain and loss be recorded; failure to remonstrate and correct is still counted a fault.
translations.idiomatic: The integrity of subject and minister requires that gain and loss be recorded; failure to remonstrate and correct is still counted a fault.

sentences.zh: 交間蒼蠅，驅扇禍戮，爵以貨重，才由貧輕，先帝舊人，無罪黜落，薦致鄉親，遍佈朝省。

translations.literal: Flies buzzing between them drove and fanned slaughter and ruin; rank grew heavy with goods, talent grew light with poverty; the late emperor's old associates, guiltless, were dismissed; kinsmen were recommended and spread throughout court and ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Flies buzzing between them drove and fanned slaughter and ruin; rank grew heavy with bribes, talent grew light with poverty; the late emperor's old associates were dismissed without cause; kinsmen were recommended and spread throughout court and ministries.

sentences.zh: 諂諛親狎者，飛榮玉除；

translations.literal: Those who flattered and drew close soared in glory upon the jade steps;
translations.idiomatic: Those who flattered and drew close soared in glory upon the jade steps;

sentences.zh: 靜立貞粹者，柴門生草。

translations.literal: those who stood quietly in pure integrity found grass growing at their wicker gates.
translations.idiomatic: those who stood quietly in pure integrity found grass growing at their wicker gates.

sentences.zh: 事先關己，雖非必行；

translations.literal: If a matter touched their interests, even if wrong it would be carried out;
translations.idiomatic: If a matter touched their interests, even if wrong it would be carried out;

sentences.zh: 若不諮詢，雖是必抑。

translations.literal: if they were not consulted, even if right it would be suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: if they were not consulted, even if right it would be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 海內遠近，人誰不知，未解執事，不加斧鉞，遂致先帝有殺弟之名，醜聲遺于君父，格以古義，豈得為忠！

translations.literal: Near and far within the realm, who does not know? Without understanding the matter, you did not apply axe and halberd, and thus left the late emperor with the name of killing his younger brother—a foul reputation bequeathed to ruler and father. Measured by ancient right, how can this be called loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Near and far within the realm, who does not know? Without understanding the matter, you did not apply axe and halberd, and thus left the late emperor with the name of killing his younger brother—a foul reputation bequeathed to ruler and father. Measured by ancient right, how can this be called loyalty!

sentences.zh: 先帝崩殂，若無天地，理痛常情，便應赴泣。

translations.literal: When the late emperor passed away, it was as though Heaven and Earth had vanished; by the logic of common feeling one ought to have rushed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor passed away, it was as though Heaven and Earth had vanished; by ordinary human feeling one ought to have rushed to weep.

sentences.zh: 但兄弟枉酷，已陷讒細，孤子已下，復觸姦機。

translations.literal: But my brothers suffered cruel injustice and had already fallen into slander and petty plots; I and those below me again touched the machinery of treachery.
translations.idiomatic: But my brothers suffered cruel injustice and had already fallen into slander and petty plots; I and those below me again touched the machinery of treachery.

sentences.zh: 是以望陵墳而摧裂，想鑾旂而抽慟。

translations.literal: Therefore gazing at the imperial tombs I am torn apart; thinking of the imperial carriage I break into sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore gazing at the imperial tombs I am torn apart; thinking of the imperial carriage I break into sobs.

sentences.zh: 雖復才違寄寵，而地屬負荷，顧命之辰，曾不見及。

translations.literal: Though my talent fell short of the trust placed in me, my position was one of burden; at the hour of the deathbed charge I was not included at all.
translations.idiomatic: Though my talent fell short of the trust placed in me, my position was one of burden; at the hour of the deathbed charge I was not included at all.

sentences.zh: 分崩之際，詔出兩豎，天誘其衷，得居乎外。

translations.literal: At the moment of collapse the edict came from two lackeys; Heaven guided my heart, and I was able to remain outside.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of collapse the edict came from two lackeys; Heaven guided my heart, and I was able to remain outside.

sentences.zh: 若受制群邪，則玉石同碎矣！

translations.literal: Had I been subject to that pack of villains, jade and stone would have been shattered together!
translations.idiomatic: Had I been subject to that pack of villains, jade and stone would have been shattered together!

sentences.zh: 以宇宙之基，一旦受制卑瑣，劉氏家國，使小人處分，終古以來，未有斯酷。

translations.literal: For the foundation of the cosmos, to be suddenly subject to base and petty men; the Liu house and state left to small men to dispose of—since antiquity there has never been such cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: For the foundation of the realm to be suddenly subject to base and petty men; the Liu house and state left to small men to dispose of—since antiquity there has never been such cruelty.

sentences.zh: 昔石顯、曹節，方今為優，而望之、仲舉，由以致弊。

translations.literal: Of old Shi Xian and Cao Jie—today's villains would be their betters; yet even Wang Wangzhi and Chen Fan, through their efforts, led to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Of old Shi Xian and Cao Jie—today's villains would be their betters; yet even Wang Wangzhi and Chen Fan, through their efforts, led to ruin.

sentences.zh: 至於遭逢醜慝，豈有古今者乎！

translations.literal: As for meeting foul and wicked men—is there any difference between ancient and modern!
translations.idiomatic: As for meeting foul and wicked men—is there any difference between ancient and modern!

sentences.zh: 諸賢胄籍冠冕，世曆忠貞，位非恩樹，勳豈寵結，憂國勤王，社稷之鎮，豈可含縱讒凶，坐觀傾覆。

translations.literal: You worthy men bear noble pedigrees and caps and sashes, generation after generation loyal and steadfast; your posts were not planted by favor, your merit not tied to patronage. You worry for the state and serve the throne—the anchors of the altars of soil and grain. How can you tolerate and indulge slander and villainy, sitting by and watching collapse?
translations.idiomatic: You worthy men bear noble pedigrees, generation after generation loyal and steadfast; your posts were not planted by favor, your merit not tied to patronage. You worry for the state and serve the throne—the anchors of the altars of soil and grain. How can you tolerate and indulge slander and villainy, sitting by and watching collapse?

sentences.zh: 自惟宋室未殞，得以推移者，正內賴諸賢，防勒姦軌；

translations.literal: Reflecting on why the Song house has not yet perished and has been able to carry on, it is precisely because within it relies on you worthy men to guard and restrain the paths of treachery;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on why the Song house has not yet perished and has been able to carry on, it is precisely because within it relies on you worthy men to guard and restrain the paths of treachery;

sentences.zh: 外有孤子，跨據中流。

translations.literal: without, I hold the midstream.
translations.idiomatic: without, I hold the midstream.

sentences.zh: 而人非金石，何能支久，使一虧落，則本根莫庇。

translations.literal: Yet men are not metal and stone—how can they endure long? If one should fall, then the root and trunk would have no shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men are not metal and stone—how can they endure long? If one should fall, then the root and trunk would have no shelter.

sentences.zh: 當今主上沖幼，宜明典章，征虜之鎮，不見慰省，逆旅往來，尚有顧眄，骨肉何仇，逼使離隔。

translations.literal: Today's sovereign is young and tender; statutes and ordinances should be made clear. The garrison of the Campaigning General receives no comforting inquiry; travelers coming and going still receive a glance of regard—what enmity between flesh and bone forces such separation?
translations.idiomatic: Today's sovereign is young and tender; statutes and ordinances should be made clear. The garrison of the Campaigning General receives no comforting inquiry; travelers coming and going still receive a glance of regard—what enmity between flesh and bone forces such separation?

sentences.zh: 禽獸之心，橫生疑貳，經由此者，每加約截，同惡相求，有若市賈。

translations.literal: With the hearts of birds and beasts, suspicion and divided loyalty arise without cause; those who pass this way are constantly subjected to restraint and interception; the wicked seek one another out like merchants at market.
translations.idiomatic: With the hearts of birds and beasts, suspicion and divided loyalty arise without cause; those who pass this way are constantly subjected to restraint and interception; the wicked seek one another out like merchants at market.

sentences.zh: 以孤子知其情狀，恆恐以此乘之，鉗勒州郡，過見防禦。

translations.literal: Because I know their circumstances, I constantly fear they will use this to press against me, clamping down on the provinces and commanderies and guarding against me beyond all measure.
translations.idiomatic: Because I know their circumstances, I constantly fear they will use this to press against me, clamping down on the provinces and commanderies and guarding against me beyond all measure.

sentences.zh: 近遣西南二使，統內宣傳，不容恐懼，即遣啟並有別書。

translations.literal: Recently two envoys were sent southwest to proclaim the will within the command; they would not permit fear, and at once dispatched memorials with separate letters.
translations.idiomatic: Recently two envoys were sent southwest to proclaim the court's will within the command; they would not permit fear, and at once dispatched memorials with separate letters.

sentences.zh: 若以孤子有過，便應鳴鼓見伐；

translations.literal: If I am at fault, then drums should be sounded and I should be attacked openly;
translations.idiomatic: If I am at fault, then drums should be sounded and I should be attacked openly;

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，宜令各有所歸。

translations.literal: if not, each side should be allowed to go its own way.
translations.idiomatic: if not, each side should be allowed to go its own way.

sentences.zh: 與殺不辜，憲有常辟，三公之使，無罪而斬，鄙雖不肖，天子之季父，卑小主者，敢不如是乎！

translations.literal: To join in killing the innocent—statute has its fixed punishment. Envoys of the Three Excellencies were beheaded though guiltless. Though I am unworthy, as the emperor's youngest uncle, would one who demeans so small a sovereign dare do otherwise!
translations.idiomatic: To join in killing the innocent—statute has its fixed punishment. Envoys of the Three Excellencies were beheaded though guiltless. Though I am unworthy, as the emperor's youngest uncle, would one who demeans so small a sovereign dare do otherwise!

sentences.zh: 孤子承奉今上，如事先朝，夙宵恭謹，散心雲日，晦望表驛，相從江衢，有何虧違，頓至於此。

translations.literal: I have served the present emperor as I served the previous court, reverent and careful from early morning to late night, my heart open as sun and cloud; at the dark of the month and the full moon I sent reports by post and traveled together on the river roads—what breach or violation brought me suddenly to this?
translations.idiomatic: I have served the present emperor as I served the previous court, reverent and careful from early morning to late night, my heart open as sun and cloud; at the dark of the month and the full moon I sent reports by post and traveled together on the river roads—what breach or violation brought me suddenly to this?

sentences.zh: 既已甘心，其可再乎！

translations.literal: Since my heart is already resolved, how can there be a second time!
translations.idiomatic: Since my heart is already resolved, how can there be a second time!

sentences.zh: 如往來所說，以孤子納士為尤，此輩懼其身罪，豈為國計。

translations.literal: As rumor has it, my fault lies in receiving retainers—this crowd fears guilt for themselves; how is that planning for the state?
translations.idiomatic: As rumor has it, my fault lies in receiving retainers—this crowd fears guilt for themselves; how is that planning for the state?

sentences.zh: 在昔四豪，列國公子，猶博引廣納，門客三千。

translations.literal: In former times the Four Heroes, princes of rival states, still broadly drew in and widely received retainers—three thousand at their gates.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the Four Heroes, princes of rival states, still broadly drew in and widely received retainers—three thousand at their gates.

sentences.zh: 況孤子位居鼎司，捍衛畿甸，且今與昔異，鹹所知也。

translations.literal: How much more so for me, who stands in the rank of the Tripod Minister and guards the capital region—and today differs from the past, as all know.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for me, who stands in the rank of the Tripod Minister and guards the capital region—and today differs from the past, as all know.

sentences.zh: 狡虜陵掠，江、淮侵逼，主上年稚，宗室衰微，邪僭用命，親賢結舌，疆場嬰塗炭之苦，征夫有勤役之勞，瓜時不代，齊猶致禍，況長淮戍卒，歷年怨思，不務拓遠強邊，而先事國君親戚，以此求心，何事非亂。

translations.literal: Crafty barbarians raid and plunder; the Yangzi and Huai are pressed by invasion. The sovereign is young, the imperial house enfeebled; the wicked and usurping command at will, the worthy and kin hold their tongues. The frontiers suffer the torment of fire and charcoal; conscript laborers bear the toil of forced service. When the melon season passed without relief, even Qi brought disaster—how much more the long-term garrison soldiers on the Huai, nursing grievance year after year! Instead of extending the far frontier and strengthening the border, you first move against the sovereign's kin—seeking men's hearts thus, what affair would not become rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Crafty barbarians raid and plunder; the Yangzi and Huai are pressed by invasion. The sovereign is young, the imperial house enfeebled; the wicked command at will, the worthy and kin hold their tongues. The frontiers suffer fire and sword; conscript laborers bear forced toil. When the melon season passed without relief, even Qi brought disaster—how much more the long-term garrison soldiers on the Huai, nursing grievance year after year! Instead of extending the far frontier and strengthening the border, you first move against the sovereign's kin—seeking men's hearts thus, what affair would not become rebellion?

sentences.zh: 又以繕治盆壘，復致囂聲。

translations.literal: Again, because I repaired the basin ramparts, uproar was raised anew.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because I repaired the basin ramparts, uproar was raised anew.

sentences.zh: 自晉、宋之災，積貯百萬，孤子到鎮，曾不數千里，且修城池，整郭邑，為治常理，復何足致嫌邪？

translations.literal: Since the calamities of Jin and Song, stores of a million have accumulated. When I reached my post it was not even several thousand li away, and to repair city walls and put the outer towns in order is ordinary governance—how can that be grounds for suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Since the calamities of Jin and Song, stores of a million have accumulated. When I reached my post it was not even several thousand li away, and to repair city walls and put the outer towns in order is ordinary governance—how can that be grounds for suspicion?

sentences.zh: 若以中流清蕩，則任農夫不應實力強兵，作鎮姑孰，俱防寇害，豈得獨嫌於此。

translations.literal: If the midstream is to be kept clear and settled, then Ren Nongfu should not be strengthening his forces in reality; garrisoning at Gushu, both alike guarding against bandits—how can I alone be singled out for suspicion here?
translations.idiomatic: If the midstream is to be kept clear and settled, then Ren Nongfu should not be strengthening his forces in reality; garrisoning at Gushu, both alike guarding against bandits—how can I alone be singled out for suspicion here?

sentences.zh: 昔成王之明，而為流言致惑，若使金縢不開，則周公無以自保。

translations.literal: Of old King Cheng was enlightened, yet was led astray by slander; had the metal-bound casket not been opened, the Duke of Zhou would have had no way to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Of old King Cheng was enlightened, yet was led astray by slander; had the metal-bound casket not been opened, the Duke of Zhou would have had no way to preserve himself.

sentences.zh: 樂毅歸趙，不忍謀燕，況孤子禮則君臣，恩猶父子者乎！

translations.literal: Yue Yi returned to Zhao and could not bear to plot against Yan—how much more for me, where in ceremony we are monarch and subject and in kindness like father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yi returned to Zhao and could not bear to plot against Yan—how much more for me, where in ceremony we are monarch and subject and in kindness like father and son!

sentences.zh: 所以枕戈泣血，只以兄弟之仇爾。

translations.literal: Therefore I sleep upon my spear and weep blood—only for the wrong done to my brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I sleep upon my spear and weep blood—only for the wrong done to my brothers.

sentences.zh: 觀其不逞之意，豈可限量。

translations.literal: Observing their unrestrained intent, how can it be measured or limited?
translations.idiomatic: Observing their unrestrained intent, how can it be measured or limited?

sentences.zh: 設使遂其虐志，諸君欲安坐得乎！

translations.literal: If they are allowed to fulfill their cruel designs, do you gentlemen expect to sit at ease and remain untouched!
translations.idiomatic: If they are allowed to fulfill their cruel designs, do you gentlemen expect to sit at ease and remain untouched!

sentences.zh: 脣亡齒寒，理不難見。

translations.literal: When the lips are gone the teeth grow cold—the principle is not hard to see.
translations.idiomatic: When the lips are gone the teeth grow cold—the principle is not hard to see.

sentences.zh: 桂蠹必除，人邪必翦，枉突徙薪，何勞多力。

translations.literal: The worm in the cassia must be removed, wicked men must be cut down; to bend the chimney and move the fuel—what need for great force?
translations.idiomatic: The worm in the cassia must be removed, wicked men must be cut down; to bend the chimney and move the fuel—what need for great force?

sentences.zh: 望便執錄二豎，以謝冤魂，則先帝不失順悌之名，宋世無枉筆之史。

translations.literal: I hope you will at once arrest and hold the two lackeys, to appease the souls of the wronged; then the late emperor will not lose the name of filial obedience and brotherly respect, and the Song age will have no history written with a crooked brush.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will at once arrest and hold the two lackeys, to appease the souls of the wronged; then the late emperor will not lose the name of filial obedience and brotherly respect, and the Song age will have no history written with a crooked brush.

sentences.zh: 此州地居形要，路枕九江，控弦跨馬，越關而至。

translations.literal: This province occupies a strategic position; its roads rest upon the Nine Rivers. Bow in hand and mounted, one crosses the passes and arrives.
translations.idiomatic: This province occupies a strategic position; its roads rest upon the Nine Rivers. Bow in hand and mounted, one crosses the passes and arrives.

sentences.zh: 重氣輕死，排藪競出，練甲照水，總戈成林，劋此纖隸，何患不克。

translations.literal: Men who prize honor above life burst from the thickets in competition; polished armor gleams on the water, spears gathered into a forest—cutting down these petty lackeys, what fear of not prevailing?
translations.idiomatic: Men who prize honor above life burst from the thickets in competition; polished armor gleams on the water, spears gathered into a forest—cutting down these petty lackeys, what fear of not prevailing?

sentences.zh: 但千鈞之弩，不為鼷鼠發機，欲使薰蕕內辨，晉陽外息爾。

translations.literal: But a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its trigger for a tiny mouse; I wish only that fragrant and foul be distinguished within, and the alarm at Jinyang cease without.
translations.idiomatic: But a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its trigger for a tiny mouse; I wish only that fragrant and foul be distinguished within, and the alarm at Jinyang cease without.

sentences.zh: 功有所歸，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Merit has its proper recipient—is that not acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: When merit has its rightful recipient, is that not fitting!

sentences.zh: 便當投命有司，謝罪天闕，同奉溫凊，齊心庶事。

translations.literal: Then one should commit oneself to the officials, confess guilt before the imperial gate, together observe the warming and cooling of filial duty, and with one heart attend to all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Then submit yourselves to the proper authorities, make apology before the throne, together fulfill your duties to the emperor, and with one heart see to the business of state.

sentences.zh: 伊、霍之任，非君而誰；

translations.literal: The task of Yi Yin and Huo Guang—if not you, then who?
translations.idiomatic: The role of Yi Yin and Huo Guang falls to no one but you.

sentences.zh: 周、邵之職，頗以自許。

translations.literal: The offices of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao—I rather claim them for myself.
translations.idiomatic: As for the duties of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, I venture to claim them as my own.

sentences.zh: 左提右挈，無愧古人。

translations.literal: Supporting on the left and leading on the right, without shame before the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: To guide and support from either hand, with no cause for shame before the ancients.

sentences.zh: 昔平、勃剛斷，產、祿蚤誅；

translations.literal: In the past Chen Ping and Zhou Bo were resolute and decisive, and Lü Chan and Lü Lu were early put to death;
translations.idiomatic: Once Chen Ping and Zhou Bo acted with resolute decisiveness, and Lü Chan and Lü Lu were swiftly executed.

sentences.zh: 張、溫趑趄，文台扼腕。

translations.literal: Zhang and Wen hesitated and faltered, and Wentai wrung his hands in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Wen wavered and hung back, while Wen Tai could only wring his hands in despair.

sentences.zh: 事之樞機，得失俄頃，往車今轍，庶無惑焉。

translations.literal: The hinge of affairs—gain and loss in an instant; the overturned cart before, the track now—perhaps let there be no confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The turning point of affairs is won or lost in a moment; learn from the overturned cart of the past, and let there be no confusion now.

sentences.zh: 近持此意，申之沈攸，其憤難不解諸王致此！

translations.literal: Recently holding this intent, I explained it to Shen You; his rage was hard to relieve—did the princes bring this about!
translations.idiomatic: I have lately pressed this very argument upon Shen You, yet his fury could not be eased—was it the princes who brought matters to this pass!

sentences.zh: 既知禍原，銳然奮發，蓄兵厲卒，以俟同舉。

translations.literal: Having known the source of the disaster, he roused himself sharply, stored troops and sharpened soldiers, to await a common rising.
translations.idiomatic: Once the source of the calamity was clear, he roused himself to action, gathered troops and hardened his men, and waited to strike together with us.

sentences.zh: 張興世發都日，受制凶黨，揚颿直逝，遂不見遇，孤子近遣信申述姦禍，方大惆惋，追恨前迷，比者信使，每申勤款。

translations.literal: On the day Zhang Xingshi set out from the capital, he fell under control of the villainous faction, set sail straight away and fled, and thus did not receive an audience; this orphan recently sent a messenger to explain the treacherous calamity—he was deeply grieved and regretful, regretting his earlier confusion, and of late his messengers have repeatedly expressed earnest good will.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xingshi departed the capital he was held in thrall to the villainous faction and sailed straight away, so that we never met. I recently sent word laying out the treachery at hand; he was sorely grieved and full of regret for his earlier misjudgment, and of late his messengers have repeatedly pledged his earnest devotion.

sentences.zh: 王奐佐郢，兵權在握，厥督屠枉，朝野嗟痛，猶父之怨，寧可與之比肩。

translations.literal: Wang Huan as deputy in Ying—military authority in his grasp; his overseers slaughtered the innocent, and court and commons lamented in pain; resentment like that of an orphan whose father was slain—how could one stand as his equal?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan served as deputy in Ying with military authority firmly in hand; his overseers butchered the innocent, and court and commons alike groaned in anguish. With a grievance like that of an orphaned son, how could one stand shoulder to shoulder with him?

sentences.zh: 孤子此舉，增其慷慨，義之所勸，其應猶響。

translations.literal: This orphan's present action increases his ardor; where righteousness urges, the response is like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: This move of mine will only deepen his resolve; where righteousness calls, the answer comes like an echo.

sentences.zh: 諸君或未得此意，故先告懷。

translations.literal: You gentlemen may not yet grasp this intent; therefore I first disclose what is in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: You may not yet have understood my meaning; that is why I set out my thoughts here first.

sentences.zh: 徙倚一隅，遲及委問。

translations.literal: I linger in one corner, awaiting your reply to what I have entrusted here.
translations.idiomatic: I linger here, awaiting your response to what I have laid before you.

sentences.zh: 孤子哀疾尪毀，窮盡無日，庶規史鰍，死不忘本。

translations.literal: This orphan is wasted by grave illness, my days nearly spent; I only hope to take Shi Qiu as my model—dying without forgetting my origin.
translations.idiomatic: I am wasted by grave illness, my days all but spent; I only hope to follow the example of Shi Qiu and die without forgetting where I came from.

sentences.zh: 臨紙荒哽，言不詮第。

translations.literal: Facing the paper I am choked and distraught; words cannot fully express my meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As I face this page I am choked with grief; words cannot say all that I mean.

sentences.zh: 大雷戍主杜道欣馳下告變。

translations.literal: Du Daoxin, garrison commander at Dalei, galloped down to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Du Daoxin, commander of the Dalei garrison, galloped down to report the uprising.

sentences.zh: 道欣至一宿，休範已至新林，朝廷震動。

translations.literal: One night after Daoxin arrived, Xiufan had already reached Xinlin; the court was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single night of Daoxin's arrival, Xiufan had already reached Xinlin, and the court was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 平南將軍齊王出次新亭壘，領軍將軍劉勔、前兗州刺史沈懷明據石頭，征北將軍張永屯白下，衛將軍袁粲、中軍褚淵、尚書左僕射劉秉等入衛殿省。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the South, the Prince of Qi, went out and encamped at the Xinting rampart; the General-in-Chief Liu Yan and the former Inspector of Yan Province Shen Huaiming held Shitou; the General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Yong encamped at Baixia; the Guard General Yuan Can, Central Army commander Chu Yuan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Bing, and others entered the palace to guard the halls.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, General Who Pacifies the South, marched out and encamped at the Xinting rampart; General-in-Chief Liu Yan and former Yanzhou Inspector Shen Huaiming held Shitou; General Who Pacifies the North Zhang Yong encamped at Baixia; Guard General Yuan Can, Central Army commander Chu Yuan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Bing, and others entered the palace precincts to defend the throne.

sentences.zh: 時事起倉卒，不暇得更處分，開南北二武庫，隨將士意取。

translations.literal: As the affair arose in sudden haste, there was no leisure for further arrangements; the northern and southern armories were opened, and the officers and men took arms as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: The crisis erupted so suddenly that there was no time for further dispositions; the northern and southern armories were thrown open, and officers and men took weapons as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 休範于新林步上，及新亭壘，自臨城南，於臨滄囗上，以數十人自衛。

translations.literal: Xiufan marched from Xinlin, reached the Xinting rampart, personally appeared south of the city, and on the Lincang □ above guarded himself with several dozen men.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan marched up from Xinlin to the Xinting rampart, appeared in person south of the city, and on the Lincang □ above kept only several dozen men as his guard.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉黃回見其可乘，乃偽往請降，並宣齊王意旨，休範大悅，以二子德宣、德嗣付回與為質，至即斬之。

translations.literal: Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Huang Hui saw that he could be taken advantage of; he therefore feigned going to offer surrender and declared the Prince of Qi's intent as well. Xiufan was greatly pleased and gave his two sons Dexuan and Desi to Hui as hostages—and upon arrival Hui at once executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Huang Hui saw his opportunity, feigned surrender, and proclaimed the Prince of Qi's terms as well. Xiufan was overjoyed and handed over his two sons Dexuan and Desi to Hui as hostages—and Hui beheaded them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 回與越騎校尉張敬兒直前斬休範首，持還，左右並奔散。

translations.literal: Hui and Colonel of Rapid Cavalry Zhang Jinger charged straight forward and cut off Xiufan's head, carried it back, and his attendants all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Colonel of Rapid Cavalry Zhang Jinger charged straight in and cut off Xiufan's head, then carried it back; his attendants all fled and scattered.

sentences.zh: 初，休範自新林分遣同黨杜耳、丁文豪、杜墨蠡等，直向朱雀。

translations.literal: Initially, Xiufan from Xinlin separately dispatched his accomplices Du Er, Ding Wenhao, Du Mol, and others straight toward Zhuque.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiufan had sent his accomplices Du Er, Ding Wenhao, Du Mol, and others straight toward Zhuque from Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 休範雖死，墨蠡等不相知聞。

translations.literal: Though Xiufan was dead, Mol and the others did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiufan was already dead, Mol and the others had no word of it.

sentences.zh: 王道隆率羽林兵在朱雀門內，聞賊至，急召劉勔。

translations.literal: Wang Daolong led the Feathered Forest troops inside Zhuque Gate; hearing the rebels had arrived, he urgently summoned Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong was inside Zhuque Gate with the Feathered Forest troops; when he heard the rebels were coming, he urgently summoned Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 勔自石頭來赴，仍進桁南，戰敗，死之。

translations.literal: Yan came from Shitou to answer the call, then advanced south of the floating bridge, was defeated, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yan came from Shitou to answer the summons, advanced south of the floating bridge, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 墨蠡等乘勝直入朱雀門，王道隆為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Mol and the others seized the victory and entered Zhuque Gate directly; Wang Daolong was killed by the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mol and the others pressed their advantage and burst straight through Zhuque Gate; Wang Daolong was slain by the rebel soldiery.

sentences.zh: 墨蠡等唱：「太尉至。」

translations.literal: Mol and the others proclaimed: "The Grand Marshal has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Mol and the others shouted: "The Grand Marshal has arrived."

sentences.zh: 休範之死也，齊王遣隊主陳靈寶齎首詣臺，道逢賊，棄首於水，挺身得達。

translations.literal: When Xiufan died, the Prince of Qi sent squad leader Chen Lingbao carrying the head to the capital; on the road he encountered rebels, cast the head into the water, and bare-bodied reached safety.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiufan fell, the Prince of Qi sent squad leader Chen Lingbao to carry the head to the capital; on the road he ran into the rebels, threw the head into the water, and escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 雖唱云已平，而無以為據，眾愈疑惑。

translations.literal: Though the cry said the matter was settled, there was nothing to serve as proof; the crowd grew ever more doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Though the shout claimed the crisis was over, there was nothing to prove it, and the people grew only more uncertain.

sentences.zh: 張永棄眾於白下，沈懷明於石頭奔散，撫軍典籤茅恬開東府納賊。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong abandoned his troops at Baixia; Shen Huaiming scattered and fled at Shitou; Mao Tian, chief clerk of the Pacification Headquarters, opened the Eastern Quarter and admitted the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong abandoned his men at Baixia; Shen Huaiming broke and fled at Shitou; Mao Tian, chief clerk of the Pacification Headquarters, opened the Eastern Quarter and let the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 墨蠡徑至杜姥宅，中書舍人孫千齡開囗明門出降，宮省恇擾，無復固志。

translations.literal: Mol went straight to the Du Lao residence; Sun Qianling, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, opened the □ming Gate and surrendered; the palace offices panicked and no longer held firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Mol went straight to the Du Lao residence; Sun Qianling, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, opened the □ming Gate and surrendered; panic seized the palace offices, and no one held firm.

sentences.zh: 時庫藏賞賜已盡，皇太后、太妃剔取宮內金銀器物以充用。

translations.literal: By then the treasuries' rewards had been exhausted; the Empress Dowager and the Grand Consort scraped together gold and silver objects from within the palace to make up the shortage.
translations.idiomatic: By then the treasury rewards had run out; the Empress Dowager and the Grand Consort stripped gold and silver vessels from within the palace to meet the need.

sentences.zh: 羽林監陳顯達率所領於杜姥宅與墨蠡戰，破之。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Chen Xianda led his command at the Du Lao residence to fight Mol and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, led his troops against Mol at the Du Lao residence and routed him.

sentences.zh: 至宣陽御道，諸賊一時奔散，斬墨蠡、文豪及同黨姜伯玉、柳中虔、任天助等。

translations.literal: Reaching the Xuanyang imperial avenue, all the rebels fled at once; Mol, Wenhao, and their accomplices Jiang Boyu, Liu Zhongqian, and Ren Tianzhu were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuanyang imperial avenue the rebels broke and fled all at once; Mol, Wenhao, and their accomplices Jiang Boyu, Liu Zhongqian, and Ren Tianzhu were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 許公輿走還新茶，村民斬送之。

translations.literal: Xu Gongyu fled back to Xinchá; villagers beheaded him and delivered his head.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gongyu fled back toward Xinchá; local villagers beheaded him and sent in his head.

sentences.zh: 晉熙王燮自夏口遣軍平尋陽，德嗣弟青牛、智藏並伏誅。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Jinxi from Xiakou dispatched troops to pacify Xunyang; Desi's younger brothers Qingniu and Zhizang were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Jinxi sent troops from Xiakou to pacify Xunyang; Desi's younger brothers Qingniu and Zhizang were both put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔建康、秣陵二縣收斂諸軍死者，并殺賊屍，並加藏埋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the two counties of Jiankang and Moling to gather the dead from the various armies, together with the corpses of the slain rebels, and bury them all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the counties of Jiankang and Moling to collect the dead from the armies and the slain rebels alike and give them all proper burial.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：語有之，投鼠而忌器，信矣。

translations.literal: The historian writes: There is a saying—when casting at a rat, one fears hitting the vessel—and how true it is.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: There is a saying that when you throw at a rat you must beware of hitting the vessel—and how true that is.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫、王道隆專用主命，臣行君道，識義之徒，咸思戮以馬劍。

translations.literal: Ruan Tianfu and Wang Daolong wielded the sovereign's mandate for their own ends, minister acting the sovereign's part; men who knew righteousness all thought to slay them with the horse-sword.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tianfu and Wang Daolong monopolized the sovereign's authority and acted the ruler's part themselves; every man who understood righteousness wished to cut them down with the ceremonial sword.

sentences.zh: 休範馳兵象魏，矢及君屋，忠臣義士，莫不銜膽爭先。

translations.literal: Xiufan drove his troops to the imperial watchtower; arrows reached the ruler's roof; loyal ministers and righteous men—none failed to hold their gall between their teeth and vie to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan drove his army to the imperial gate-tower; arrows struck the ruler's hall; loyal ministers and righteous men all clenched their resolve and raced to the fore.

sentences.zh: 夫以邪附君，猶或自免，況於仗正順以爭主哉！

translations.literal: If even those who cleave to the sovereign through wickedness may sometimes save themselves, how much less when one relies on righteousness and legitimacy to contend for the throne!
translations.idiomatic: If even those who clung to the throne through wickedness might sometimes save themselves, how much less could one who relied on righteousness and legitimacy to seize it hope to escape!
